policy: A verse is kept for a record where it speaks of that very record, by a title, a description, another name or a pronoun, and the text itself says who is meant: in the verse, in the lines around it, or in a statement of the same book. What only tradition or a later reading identifies is not kept. A people is kept where the verse speaks of the nation or the tribe as a body and not of the man it is named after or of the land alone. A reading both models gave is kept as it stands; where they differed the third reading says why it kept the verse. The word that stands for the record is annotated where it is a noun or a name and both readings point at the same word.

readings.first: 'even unto the children of Ammon: for the border of the children of Ammon was strong': the Ammonites as a nation whose border Israel reached.
readings.second: 'even unto the children of Ammon: for the border of the children of Ammon was strong': a nation with a defended border beside Sihon's kingdom.

readings.first: 'the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab': Moabite women of the nation, not the man Moab.
readings.second: 'the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab': the women of the nation, who 'called the people unto the sacrifices of their gods' (25:2).

readings.first: 'These are the families of Manasseh, and those that were numbered of them, fifty and two thousand': the tribe's census.
readings.second: 'These are the families of Manasseh, and those that were numbered of them, fifty and two thousand': the tribe's clans counted.

readings.first: 'These are the families of the sons of Ephraim according to those that were numbered of them, thirty and two thousand': the tribe's families counted.
readings.second: 'These are the families of the sons of Ephraim according to those that were numbered of them, thirty and two thousand': the tribe counted by clans.

readings.first: 'These are the sons of Benjamin after their families: and they that were numbered of them were forty and five thousand and six hundred': the tribe counted.
readings.second: 'These are the sons of Benjamin after their families: and they that were numbered of them were forty and five thousand': the tribe numbered.

readings.first: 'the families of the sons of Asher... numbered... fifty and three thousand and four hundred': the tribe counted by families.
readings.second: 'These are the families of the sons of Asher ... fifty and three thousand and four hundred': the tribe numbered by families.

readings.first: 'These are the families of Naphtali according to their families: and they that were numbered of them were forty and five thousand': the tribe's census.
readings.second: 'These are the families of Naphtali according to their families: and they that were numbered of them were forty and five thousand'.

readings.first: 'delivered out of the thousands of Israel, a thousand of every tribe': the nation's divisions supplying troops.
readings.second: 'delivered out of the thousands of Israel, a thousand of every tribe, twelve thousand armed': the nation's army divisions.

readings.first: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad had a very great multitude of cattle': the tribe as a body owning herds.
readings.second: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad had a very great multitude of cattle': the tribes seeing Jazer and Gilead.

readings.first: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad had a very great multitude of cattle': the tribe as owner of herds.
readings.second: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad had a very great multitude of cattle': the tribe seeking Gilead.

readings.first: 'The children of Gad and the children of Reuben came and spake unto Moses': the tribe acting as a body.
readings.second: 'The children of Gad and the children of Reuben came and spake unto Moses': the tribes petitioning as a body.

readings.first: 'The children of Gad and the children of Reuben came and spake unto Moses': the tribe as speakers.
readings.second: 'The children of Gad and the children of Reuben came and spake unto Moses': the tribe asking for the land east of Jordan.

readings.first: 'the country which the LORD smote before the congregation of Israel': the nation before whom the land was struck.
readings.second: 'the country which the LORD smote before the congregation of Israel': the nation before whom the land was conquered.

readings.first: 'Moses said unto the children of Gad and to the children of Reuben, Shall your brethren go to war': the tribe addressed.
readings.second: 'Moses said unto the children of Gad and to the children of Reuben, Shall your brethren go to war': the tribes addressed.

readings.first: 'Moses said unto the children of Gad and to the children of Reuben, Shall your brethren go to war, and shall ye sit here?': the tribe addressed.
readings.second: 'Moses said unto the children of Gad and to the children of Reuben, Shall your brethren go to war, and shall ye sit here?'

readings.first: 'the children of Gad and the children of Reuben spake unto Moses': the tribe speaking.
readings.second: 'the children of Gad and the children of Reuben spake unto Moses, saying, Thy servants will do': the tribes answering as a body.

readings.first: 'the children of Gad and the children of Reuben spake unto Moses, saying, Thy servants will do as my lord commandeth': the tribe answers.
readings.second: 'the children of Gad and the children of Reuben spake unto Moses... Thy servants will do as my lord commandeth'.

readings.first: 'If the children of Gad and the children of Reuben will pass with you over Jordan, every man armed': the tribe's fighting men.
readings.second: 'If the children of Gad and the children of Reuben will pass with you over Jordan, every man armed': the tribes' warriors and their possession.

readings.first: 'If the children of Gad and the children of Reuben will pass with you over Jordan... then ye shall give them the land of Gilead': the tribe as party.
readings.second: 'If the children of Gad and the children of Reuben will pass with you over Jordan, every man armed to battle... give them the land of Gilead'.

readings.first: 'the children of Gad and the children of Reuben answered, saying... so will we do': the tribe answering Moses.
readings.second: 'the children of Gad and the children of Reuben answered, saying... so will we do': the tribes answering Moses as a body.

readings.words: the children of Gad and the children of Reuben
readings.first: 'the children of Gad and the children of Reuben answered': the two tribes as a body reply to Moses.
readings.second: 'the children of Gad and the children of Reuben answered... so will we do': the tribe negotiating its possession with Moses, not the man Reuben.

readings.first: 'the children of Gad built Dibon, and Ataroth, and Aroer': the tribe building cities.
readings.second: 'the children of Gad built Dibon, and Ataroth, and Aroer': the tribe building cities in its territory.

readings.first: 'the children of Reuben built Heshbon, and Elealeh': the tribe rebuilds cities.
readings.second: 'the children of Reuben built Heshbon, and Elealeh, and Kirjathaim': the tribe building cities in its territory.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Gad
readings.first: 'the tribe of the children of Gad according to the house of their fathers, have received their inheritance': the tribe (Hebrew: the Gadite) receiving its share.
readings.second: 'the tribe of the children of Gad according to the house of their fathers, have received their inheritance': word 14 is the gentilic 'the Gadite'.

readings.first: 'half the tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance': a tribal half as a body.
readings.second: 'half the tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance': the half tribe east of Jordan, beside Reuben and Gad.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Simeon
readings.first: 'of the tribe of the children of Simeon, Shemuel the son of Ammihud': the tribe's prince for dividing the land.
readings.second: 'of the tribe of the children of Simeon, Shemuel the son of Ammihud': the tribe's prince for dividing the land.

readings.first: 'Of the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad the son of Chislon': the tribe's appointed man.
readings.second: 'Of the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad the son of Chislon': the tribe's representative for dividing the land.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Manasseh
readings.first: 'The prince of the children of Joseph, for the tribe of the children of Manasseh, Hanniel': the tribe's prince.
readings.second: 'for the tribe of the children of Manasseh, Hanniel the son of Ephod': the tribe's prince for dividing the land; 'Joseph' (3) is the wider house.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Ephraim
readings.first: 'the prince of the tribe of the children of Ephraim, Kemuel': the tribe with its prince.
readings.second: 'the prince of the tribe of the children of Ephraim, Kemuel': a tribal leader for dividing the land.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Zebulun
readings.first: 'the prince of the tribe of the children of Zebulun, Elizaphan the son of Parnach': the tribe's prince for dividing the land.
readings.second: 'the prince of the tribe of the children of Zebulun, Elizaphan the son of Parnach': the tribe's prince for dividing the land.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Asher
readings.first: 'the prince of the tribe of the children of Asher, Ahihud the son of Shelomi': the tribe's prince.
readings.second: 'the prince of the tribe of the children of Asher, Ahihud': the tribe's representative.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Naphtali
readings.first: 'the prince of the tribe of the children of Naphtali, Pedahel the son of Ammihud': the tribe's prince for dividing the land.
readings.second: 'the prince of the tribe of the children of Naphtali, Pedahel the son of Ammihud': a prince to divide the land.

readings.first: 'distress them not, nor meddle with them' and 'the land of the children of Ammon' given to 'the children of Lot': the nation and its possession.
readings.second: 'distress them not, nor meddle with them ... the land of the children of Ammon': a people Israel is not to fight, holding a land given to the children of Lot.

readings.first: 'the land of the children of Ammon thou camest not': the land is named as belonging to the nation, the children of Ammon, which Israel left alone.
readings.second: 'the land of the children of Ammon thou camest not': the territory is named as belonging to the people, the children of Ammon.

readings.first: 'Rabbath of the children of Ammon': the city is named as the city of the Ammonite nation.
readings.second: 'in Rabbath of the children of Ammon': the city is identified as the people's city, the children of Ammon as a body.

readings.first: 'the border of the children of Ammon': the boundary belongs to the nation, the children of Ammon.
readings.second: 'the river Jabbok, which is the border of the children of Ammon': the border of a people's territory, the children of Ammon as a nation.

readings.first: 'the LORD separated the tribe of Levi, to bear the ark': the tribe set apart.
readings.second: 'the LORD separated the tribe of Levi, to bear the ark of the covenant of the LORD': the tribe set apart.

readings.first: 'Moses spake in the ears of all the congregation of Israel the words of this song': the nation as audience.
readings.second: 'Moses spake in the ears of all the congregation of Israel the words of this song': the assembled nation.

readings.first: 'Moses commanded us a law, even the inheritance of the congregation of Jacob': 'Jacob' here names the assembly, the nation (called Israel in v.5), not the man.
readings.second: 'a law, even the inheritance of the congregation of Jacob': Jacob names the assembled people, beside 'the tribes of Israel' in 33:5.

readings.first: 'they are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh': the multitudes of the two Joseph tribes in the blessing on Joseph.
readings.second: 'they are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh': Joseph's horns are the tribe's multitudes, not the man.

readings.first: 'the children of Reuben, and the children of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh, passed over armed before the children of Israel': the tribe's fighting men.
readings.second: 'the children of Reuben, and the children of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh, passed over armed': the tribes' warriors crossing Jordan.

readings.first: 'the children of Reuben, and the children of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh, passed over armed': the tribal half as a body.
readings.second: 'the children of Reuben, and the children of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh, passed over armed before the children of Israel'.

readings.first: 'the children of Reuben, and the children of Gad, and half the tribe of Manasseh, passed over armed': a tribal army.
readings.second: 'the children of Reuben... passed over armed before the children of Israel': the tribe's armed men crossing the Jordan.

readings.first: 'make the camp of Israel a curse, and trouble it': the nation encamped, warned against being made a curse.
readings.second: 'make the camp of Israel a curse, and trouble it': the nation's camp at Jericho.

readings.first: 'all Israel, and their elders, and officers' stood by the ark, and 'bless the people of Israel': the nation as a body.
readings.second: 'all Israel, and their elders, and officers, and their judges, stood' and 'bless the people of Israel': the assembled nation at Ebal and Gerizim.

readings.first: Joshua read the law 'before all the congregation of Israel, with the women, and the little ones': the assembled nation.
readings.second: Joshua read the law 'before all the congregation of Israel, with the women, and the little ones': the assembled nation.

readings.first: 'Moses... gave it for a possession unto the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh': a tribal half receiving land.
readings.second: 'gave it for a possession unto the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh': the tribe receiving land.

readings.first: 'the king of Hebron, one' in the list of kings Joshua smote is the king of Hebron named Hoham in 10:3 and slain among the five (10:23).
readings.second: 'the king of Hebron' stands with the kings of Jerusalem, Jarmuth, Lachish and Eglon in the order of 10:3, where he is Hoham; 10:37 speaks of a later king of Hebron too.

readings.first: 'the king of Lachish, one' in the list of kings Joshua smote is 'Japhia king of Lachish' of 10:3, one of the five kings of 10:23.
readings.second: 'the king of Lachish' is listed with the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth and Eglon, the five of 10:3 and 10:23, where the king of Lachish is Japhia.

readings.first: 'The king of Madon, one' in the list of kings Joshua smote is the king of Madon of 11:1, 'Jobab king of Madon'.
readings.second: 'The king of Madon' among the kings Joshua smote is Jobab, whom JOS 11:1 calls 'Jobab king of Madon' and whose allied kings Joshua took and smote (11:12).

readings.first: 'the king of Megiddo, one' prints the record's own designation, king of Megiddo.
readings.second: 'the king of Megiddo, one' is this very king, listed among the kings Joshua smote (12:7).

readings.words: the king of Jokneam of Carmel
readings.first: 'the king of Jokneam of Carmel, one' prints the record's own designation, king of Jokneam.
readings.second: 'the king of Jokneam of Carmel, one' is this very king, listed among the kings Joshua smote (12:7).

readings.first: 'unto the border of the children of Ammon': the nation whose border ends Sihon's cities.
readings.second: 'unto the border of the children of Ammon': the frontier of the nation, beside Sihon king of the Amorites.

readings.first: 'unto the tribes of Levi he gave none inheritance': the tribe has no land share.
readings.second: 'unto the tribes of Levi he gave none inheritance; the sacrifices of the LORD... are their inheritance': the tribe as a body.

readings.first: 'the border of the children of Reuben... the inheritance of the children of Reuben after their families': the tribe's allotment.
readings.second: 'the border of the children of Reuben... the inheritance of the children of Reuben after their families': the tribe's allotted territory.

readings.first: 'Moses gave inheritance unto the tribe of Gad, even unto the children of Gad according to their families': the tribe receiving an inheritance.
readings.second: 'Moses gave inheritance unto the tribe of Gad, even unto the children of Gad according to their families': both phrases name the tribe.

readings.first: 'half the land of the children of Ammon': the territory belongs to the Ammonite nation, named as a body.
readings.second: 'half the land of the children of Ammon, unto Aroer that is before Rabbah': the land is named as the people's.

readings.first: 'This is the inheritance of the children of Gad after their families, the cities, and their villages': the tribe's inheritance.
readings.second: 'This is the inheritance of the children of Gad after their families, the cities, and their villages': the tribe's inheritance.

readings.words: the half tribe of the children of Manasseh
readings.first: 'Moses gave inheritance unto the half tribe of Manasseh... the possession of the half tribe of the children of Manasseh by their families': the tribal half.
readings.second: 'Moses gave inheritance unto the half tribe of Manasseh: and this was the possession of the half tribe of the children of Manasseh by their families'.

readings.first: 'unto the tribe of Levi Moses gave not any inheritance': the tribe as a body.
readings.second: 'unto the tribe of Levi Moses gave not any inheritance: the LORD God of Israel was their inheritance'.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Judah
readings.first: 'the lot of the tribe of the children of Judah by their families': the tribe's allotment, its families.
readings.second: 'the lot of the tribe of the children of Judah by their families': the tribe's allotment.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Judah
readings.first: 'the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Judah according to their families': the tribe and its families.
readings.second: 'the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Judah according to their families': the tribe's inheritance.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Judah
readings.first: 'the uttermost cities of the tribe of the children of Judah': the tribe as owner of the cities listed, its allotment.
readings.second: 'the uttermost cities of the tribe of the children of Judah': the tribe's cities in its allotment.

readings.first: 'the border of the children of Ephraim according to their families... their inheritance': the tribe's allotment; the people, not the land, are named.
readings.second: 'the border of the children of Ephraim according to their families... the border of their inheritance': the tribe's allotted territory.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Ephraim
readings.first: 'This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Ephraim by their families': the tribe and its inheritance.
readings.second: 'This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Ephraim by their families': the tribe's inheritance.

readings.first: 'the separate cities for the children of Ephraim were among the inheritance of the children of Manasseh': the tribe holding cities.
readings.second: 'the separate cities for the children of Ephraim were among the inheritance of the children of Manasseh': cities belonging to the tribe.

readings.first: 'separate cities for the children of Ephraim were among the inheritance of the children of Manasseh': the tribe's inheritance.
readings.second: 'the separate cities for the children of Ephraim were among the inheritance of the children of Manasseh': the tribe's inheritance.

readings.first: 'a lot for... the children of Helek': a Manasseh clan receiving land by families.
readings.second: 'a lot for the rest of the children of Manasseh by their families... for the children of Helek': the Helekite family receiving land.

readings.first: 'a lot for... the children of Shemida': a family of Manasseh, a clan receiving its share 'by their families'; the verse lists no gentilic form.
readings.second: 'a lot for... the children of Shemida... by their families': the clan receiving its lot, not Shemida himself.

readings.first: 'a lot for... the children of Shechem': a family of Manasseh receiving a lot 'by their families'; here the ancestor's name, not a town.
readings.second: 'a lot for... the children of Shechem... by their families': the clan of Manasseh receiving its lot, not the man.

readings.first: 'the daughters of Manasseh had an inheritance among his sons: and the rest of Manasseh's sons had the land of Gilead': the tribe's women and remaining families, generations after the man.
readings.second: 'the daughters of Manasseh had an inheritance among his sons: and the rest of Manasseh's sons had the land of Gilead': descendants sharing the tribal allotment (17:5).

readings.first: 'Tappuah on the border of Manasseh belonged to the children of Ephraim': the tribe owning a town.
readings.second: 'Tappuah on the border of Manasseh belonged to the children of Ephraim': the town is assigned to the tribe.

readings.first: 'the children of Manasseh could not drive out the inhabitants of those cities': the tribe as actors.
readings.second: 'the children of Manasseh could not drive out the inhabitants of those cities': the tribe in the conquest.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Benjamin
readings.first: 'the lot of the tribe of the children of Benjamin came up according to their families': the tribe's lot.
readings.second: 'the lot of the tribe of the children of Benjamin came up according to their families': the tribe's lot.

readings.first: 'Kirjathjearim, a city of the children of Judah': a city belonging to the tribe as a body, marking the boundary.
readings.second: 'Kirjathjearim, a city of the children of Judah': a city belonging to the tribe.

readings.first: 'This was the inheritance of the children of Benjamin... according to their families': the tribe's inheritance.
readings.second: 'This was the inheritance of the children of Benjamin ... according to their families': the tribe's inheritance.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Benjamin
readings.first: 'the cities of the tribe of the children of Benjamin according to their families': the tribe's cities.
readings.second: 'the cities of the tribe of the children of Benjamin according to their families': the tribe's cities.

readings.first: 'This is the inheritance of the children of Benjamin according to their families': the tribe's inheritance.
readings.second: 'This is the inheritance of the children of Benjamin according to their families': the tribe's inheritance.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Simeon
readings.first: 'the second lot came forth to Simeon, even for the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families': the tribe's lot.
readings.second: 'the second lot came forth to Simeon, even for the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families': the tribe's inheritance.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Simeon
readings.first: 'This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families': the tribe's allotment.
readings.second: 'This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Simeon according to their families': the tribe's allotted villages.

readings.first: 'the children of Simeon had their inheritance within the inheritance of them': the tribe took possession within Judah's portion.
readings.second: 'the inheritance of the children of Simeon... the children of Simeon had their inheritance within the inheritance of them': the tribe inheriting inside Judah.

readings.first: 'the third lot came up for the children of Zebulun according to their families': the tribe's lot.
readings.second: 'the third lot came up for the children of Zebulun according to their families': the tribe receiving its lot.

readings.first: 'This is the inheritance of the children of Zebulun according to their families': the tribe's allotment.
readings.second: 'This is the inheritance of the children of Zebulun according to their families': the tribe's cities and villages.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Asher
readings.first: 'the fifth lot came out for the tribe of the children of Asher according to their families': the tribe's lot.
readings.second: 'the fifth lot came out for the tribe of the children of Asher according to their families': the tribe's lot.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Asher
readings.first: 'the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Asher according to their families': the tribe's inheritance.
readings.second: 'This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Asher according to their families': the tribe's inheritance.

readings.first: 'The sixth lot came out to the children of Naphtali, even for the children of Naphtali according to their families': the tribe receives its lot.
readings.second: 'The sixth lot came out to the children of Naphtali, even for the children of Naphtali according to their families'.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Naphtali
readings.first: 'the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Naphtali according to their families': the tribe's inheritance.
readings.second: 'This is the inheritance of the tribe of the children of Naphtali according to their families, the cities and their villages'.

readings.words: the rest of the children of Kohath
readings.first: 'the rest of the children of Kohath had by lot... ten cities': the remaining Kohathite families receive cities.
readings.second: 'the rest of the children of Kohath had by lot... ten cities': the clan receiving cities, after 'the families of the Kohathites' in 21:4.

readings.first: 'out of the half tribe of Manasseh, ten cities': a tribal half giving cities to the Kohathites.
readings.second: 'out of the half tribe of Manasseh, ten cities': cities given to Kohath out of the tribe's inheritance.

readings.first: 'the children of Gershon had by lot out of the families of the tribe of Issachar... thirteen cities': the clan receiving cities.
readings.second: 'the children of Gershon had by lot out of the families of the tribe of Issachar... thirteen cities': the clan receiving cities.

readings.first: 'out of the half tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities': a tribal half giving cities to Gershon's sons.
readings.second: 'out of the half tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities': the tribe's inheritance yielding cities to Gershon.

readings.first: 'The children of Merari had out of the tribe of Reuben, and out of the tribe of Gad, and out of the tribe of Zebulun, twelve cities': the tribe giving cities to Levites.
readings.second: 'The children of Merari by their families had out of the tribe of Reuben, and out of the tribe of Gad': Levitical cities taken from the tribe's lot.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Judah
readings.first: 'they gave out of the tribe of the children of Judah, and out of the tribe of the children of Simeon, these cities': the tribe gives cities to the Levites.
readings.second: 'they gave out of the tribe of the children of Judah ... these cities': cities given from the tribe's lot.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Simeon
readings.first: 'they gave out of the tribe of the children of Judah, and out of the tribe of the children of Simeon, these cities': the tribe gives cities.
readings.second: 'they gave... out of the tribe of the children of Simeon, these cities': cities given to the Levites from the tribe's land.

readings.first: 'the families of the Kohathites, who were of the children of Levi': the Aaronites are of the tribe of Levi, which receives the first lot.
readings.second: 'the children of Aaron, being of the families of the Kohathites, who were of the children of Levi': the tribe; 'Kohathite' (9) names a clan within it.

readings.words: the families of the children of Kohath
readings.first: 'the families of the children of Kohath, the Levites which remained of the children of Kohath... had the cities of their lot': the clan as a body.
readings.second: 'the families of the children of Kohath, the Levites which remained of the children of Kohath, even they had the cities of their lot'.

readings.first: 'out of the half tribe of Manasseh, Tanach... and Gathrimmon': the tribal half as giver of cities.
readings.second: 'out of the half tribe of Manasseh, Tanach with her suburbs, and Gathrimmon': cities given from the tribe's inheritance.

readings.words: the families of the children of Kohath that remained
readings.first: 'for the families of the children of Kohath that remained': the clan's share of ten cities.
readings.second: 'All the cities were ten with their suburbs for the families of the children of Kohath that remained': the clan's allotment.

readings.first: 'unto the children of Gershon, of the families of the Levites... they gave Golan in Bashan': the clan receiving cities.
readings.second: 'unto the children of Gershon, of the families of the Levites... they gave Golan in Bashan': the clan receiving cities; word 8 'Levites' is the wider tribe.

readings.words: the other half tribe of Manasseh
readings.first: 'out of the other half tribe of Manasseh they gave Golan in Bashan': the tribal half as giver of cities.
readings.second: 'out of the other half tribe of Manasseh they gave Golan in Bashan': cities from the tribe's inheritance to the Gershonites.

readings.first: 'out of the tribe of Gad, Ramoth in Gilead with her suburbs': cities given from the tribe's holding; the tribe is what is named.
readings.second: 'out of the tribe of Gad, Ramoth in Gilead with her suburbs': cities given from the tribe's possession.

readings.first: 'any good thing which the LORD had spoken unto the house of Israel; all came to pass': the nation addressed by promise.
readings.second: 'any good thing which the LORD had spoken unto the house of Israel': the nation that received the land (21:43).

readings.first: 'Joshua called the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh': the tribal half summoned.
readings.second: 'Joshua called the Reubenites, and the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh': the tribe summoned and addressed as 'ye' in 22:2.

readings.words: the one half of the tribe of Manasseh
readings.first: 'to the one half of the tribe of Manasseh Moses had given possession in Bashan': the tribe divided in two halves.
readings.second: 'to the one half of the tribe of Manasseh Moses had given possession in Bashan: but unto the other half thereof gave Joshua'.

readings.first: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh returned, and departed from the children of Israel': the tribe returning home.
readings.second: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh returned... to the land of their possession': the tribes going home.

readings.first: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh returned': a tribal half departing.
readings.second: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh returned... to the land of their possession'.

readings.first: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh returned': the tribes as a body.
readings.second: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad... returned... to the land of their possession': the tribe going home to Gilead.

readings.first: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh built there an altar by Jordan': the tribe acting.
readings.second: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh built there an altar by Jordan': the tribes acting together.

readings.first: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh built there an altar': the tribal half as builders.
readings.second: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh built there an altar by Jordan'.

readings.first: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad... built there an altar by Jordan': the tribes acting together.
readings.second: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad... built there an altar by Jordan': the tribe acting as a body.

readings.first: 'Behold, the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh have built an altar': the tribe reported as builders.
readings.second: 'Behold, the children of Reuben and the children of Gad... have built an altar': the tribes reported to Israel.

readings.first: 'the half tribe of Manasseh have built an altar over against the land of Canaan': the tribal half as builders.
readings.second: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh have built an altar over against the land of Canaan'.

readings.first: 'Behold, the children of Reuben and the children of Gad... have built an altar': what Israel heard of the tribes.
readings.second: 'Behold, the children of Reuben and the children of Gad... have built an altar': the tribe reported to Israel.

readings.first: 'the children of Israel sent unto the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad, and to the half tribe of Manasseh': the tribe receiving envoys.
readings.second: 'the children of Israel sent unto the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad... Phinehas': the tribes to whom the embassy was sent.

readings.first: 'sent unto... the half tribe of Manasseh, into the land of Gilead, Phinehas': the tribal half receiving an embassy.
readings.second: 'the children of Israel sent unto the children of Reuben... and to the half tribe of Manasseh, into the land of Gilead, Phinehas'.

readings.first: 'sent unto the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad': the tribe as a body receives an embassy.
readings.second: 'the children of Israel sent unto the children of Reuben... into the land of Gilead, Phinehas': an embassy to the tribe.

readings.first: 'they came unto the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad, and to the half tribe of Manasseh': the tribe visited.
readings.second: 'they came unto the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad... unto the land of Gilead': the tribes addressed by the embassy.

readings.first: 'they came unto... the half tribe of Manasseh, unto the land of Gilead, and they spake with them': the tribal half addressed.
readings.second: 'they came unto the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad, and to the half tribe of Manasseh... and they spake with them'.

readings.first: 'they came unto the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad': the tribe addressed as a body.
readings.second: 'they came unto the children of Reuben... unto the land of Gilead, and they spake with them': the tribe addressed by the envoys.

readings.first: 'he will be wroth with the whole congregation of Israel': the nation as a body under wrath.
readings.second: 'he will be wroth with the whole congregation of Israel': the assembled nation, liable for the eastern tribes' altar.

readings.first: 'wrath fell on all the congregation of Israel' after Achan's trespass: the nation as a body.
readings.second: 'wrath fell on all the congregation of Israel' for Achan's trespass: the nation as a body.

readings.first: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh answered': the tribe answering Israel's heads.
readings.second: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh answered': the tribes replying as a body.

readings.words: the heads of the thousands of Israel
readings.first: Reuben, Gad and Manasseh spoke 'unto the heads of the thousands of Israel': the nation's divisions and their leaders.
readings.second: 'the heads of the thousands of Israel': leaders of the nation's divisions, addressed by Reuben, Gad and half Manasseh.

readings.first: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh answered': the tribal half speaks.
readings.second: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh answered, and said unto the heads of the thousands of Israel'.

readings.first: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad... answered, and said unto the heads of the thousands of Israel': the tribes speaking.
readings.second: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad... answered, and said unto the heads of the thousands of Israel': the tribe replying.

readings.first: 'ye children of Reuben and children of Gad; ye have no part in the LORD': the tribe addressed, in the speakers' imagined future.
readings.second: 'a border between us and you, ye children of Reuben and children of Gad; ye have no part in the LORD': the tribes as imagined future Israel would address them.

readings.first: 'ye children of Reuben and children of Gad; ye have no part in the LORD': the tribe addressed, with Jordan as border between.
readings.second: 'the LORD hath made Jordan a border between us and you, ye children of Reuben': the tribe addressed, with its children, as a people.

readings.first: 'the words that the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the children of Manasseh spake, it pleased them': the tribe speaking.
readings.second: 'heard the words that the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the children of Manasseh spake': the tribes' answer.

readings.first: 'heads of the thousands of Israel which were with him' heard the words: leaders of the nation's divisions.
readings.second: 'heads of the thousands of Israel which were with him': divisions of the nation, alongside the princes of the congregation.

readings.first: 'the words that the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the children of Manasseh spake, it pleased them': the tribal half as speakers.
readings.second: 'heard the words that the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the children of Manasseh spake, it pleased them': the eastern tribes.

readings.first: 'the words that the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the children of Manasseh spake': the tribes speaking.
readings.second: 'heard the words that the children of Reuben and the children of Gad... spake': the tribe's spokesmen as a body.

readings.first: 'Phinehas... said unto the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad, and to the children of Manasseh': the tribe addressed.
readings.second: 'Phinehas... said unto the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad': the tribes addressed, 'ye have not committed this trespass'.

readings.first: 'Phinehas... said unto the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad, and to the children of Manasseh': the tribal half addressed.
readings.second: 'Phinehas... said unto the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad, and to the children of Manasseh... ye have not committed this trespass'.

readings.first: 'Phinehas... said unto the children of Reuben, and to the children of Gad': the tribe addressed as a body.
readings.second: 'Phinehas... said unto the children of Reuben... ye have not committed this trespass': the tribe addressed.

readings.first: 'returned from the children of Reuben, and from the children of Gad, out of the land of Gilead': the tribe the envoys came from.
readings.second: 'returned from the children of Reuben, and from the children of Gad, out of the land of Gilead': the tribes Phinehas left.

readings.first: 'returned from the children of Reuben, and from the children of Gad': the tribes as a body, from whom the envoys return.
readings.second: 'returned from the children of Reuben, and from the children of Gad, out of the land of Gilead': the tribe in its land.

readings.words: the children of Reuben and Gad
readings.first: 'the land wherein the children of Reuben and Gad dwelt': 'Gad' (Hebrew: sons of Gad) means the tribe dwelling there, not the land.
readings.second: 'to destroy the land wherein the children of Reuben and Gad dwelt': the Gadites dwelling in their land; Hebrew repeats 'sons of Gad' (33).

readings.first: 'the land wherein the children of Reuben and Gad dwelt': the tribe's dwelling, tribe as body in view.
readings.second: 'to destroy the land wherein the children of Reuben and Gad dwelt': the tribe dwelling in its territory.

readings.first: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad called the altar Ed': the tribe naming the altar.
readings.second: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad called the altar Ed': the tribes naming their altar.

readings.first: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad called the altar Ed': the tribes act as a body.
readings.second: 'the children of Reuben and the children of Gad called the altar Ed': the tribe naming its altar.

readings.first: 'anger of the LORD was hot against Israel, and he sold them... the children of Israel served Chushanrishathaim eight years': the nation.
readings.second: 'the anger of the LORD was hot against Israel ... the children of Israel served Chushanrishathaim eight years': the nation in servitude.

readings.first: 'he gathered unto him the children of Ammon and Amalek': Eglon gathers the Ammonites as a force against Israel.
readings.second: 'he gathered unto him the children of Ammon and Amalek, and went and smote Israel': a nation allied with Eglon in war.

readings.first: 'take with thee ten thousand men of the children of Naphtali and of the children of Zebulun': the tribe supplies fighting men.
readings.second: 'take with thee ten thousand men of the children of Naphtali': the tribe's men; 'Kedeshnaphtali' (11) is a place name, not the people.

readings.first: 'And he said unto him, If now I have found grace in thy sight' is the reply to 6:16, from the one who asked 'wherewith shall I save Israel?' in 6:15, Gideon (6:13).
readings.second: 'shew me a sign that thou talkest with me' is said by Gideon, who speaks in 6:13 and 6:15 and is named again in 6:19; word 12 is 'to me'.

readings.first: 'he sent all the rest of Israel every man unto his tent, and retained those three hundred' follows the LORD's word to Gideon in 7:7 to let the others go; only the verb carries the subject.
readings.second: 'he sent all the rest of Israel' and 'the host of Midian was beneath him' carry out the LORD's word 'unto Gideon' in 7:7; word 32 is 'to him'.

readings.first: 'the children of Ammon passed over Jordan to fight also against Judah': the nation as an invading army.
readings.second: 'the children of Ammon passed over Jordan to fight also against Judah': a nation making war.

readings.first: 'from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines': the LORD names the Ammonites among the nations that oppressed Israel.
readings.second: 'Did not I deliver you ... from the children of Ammon': listed among oppressing nations with the Egyptians and Philistines.

readings.first: 'the children of Ammon were gathered together, and encamped in Gilead': the nation as an army.
readings.second: 'the children of Ammon were gathered together, and encamped in Gilead': an army of the nation.

readings.first: 'begin to fight against the children of Ammon': the Ammonites as the enemy of Gilead.
readings.second: 'What man is he that will begin to fight against the children of Ammon?': the enemy nation encamped in Gilead.

readings.first: 'the children of Ammon made war against Israel': the nation makes war.
readings.second: 'the children of Ammon made war against Israel': a nation at war.

readings.first: 'the children of Ammon made war against Israel': the nation at war, prompting the elders of Gilead.
readings.second: 'when the children of Ammon made war against Israel': the nation at war with Israel.

readings.first: 'that we may fight with the children of Ammon': the Ammonites as the enemy to be fought.
readings.second: 'that we may fight with the children of Ammon': the enemy nation.

readings.first: 'fight against the children of Ammon': the Ammonite nation as the enemy of Gilead.
readings.second: 'go with us, and fight against the children of Ammon': the enemy nation.

readings.first: 'to fight against the children of Ammon, and the LORD deliver them before me': the nation as enemy; 'them' is the same body.
readings.second: 'to fight against the children of Ammon, and the LORD deliver them before me': the enemy nation, then 'them'.

readings.first: 'nor the land of the children of Ammon': Israel did not take the land of the Ammonite nation, named beside Moab's.
readings.second: 'Israel took not away ... the land of the children of Ammon': the land named as the nation's, answering their king's claim.

readings.first: 'between the children of Israel and the children of Ammon': the LORD judges between two nations.
readings.second: 'be judge this day between the children of Israel and the children of Ammon': two nations in dispute.

readings.first: 'he passed over unto the children of Ammon': Jephthah marches against the Ammonites as a people.
readings.second: 'from Mizpeh of Gilead he passed over unto the children of Ammon': Jephthah advances against the enemy nation.

readings.first: 'deliver the children of Ammon into mine hands': the nation as enemy in a vow.
readings.second: 'If thou shalt without fail deliver the children of Ammon into mine hands': the enemy nation in battle.

readings.first: 'when I return in peace from the children of Ammon': the nation Jephthah goes to fight.
readings.second: 'when I return in peace from the children of Ammon': returning from war against the nation.

readings.first: 'passed over unto the children of Ammon to fight against them': the nation, then 'them' as a body.
readings.second: 'passed over unto the children of Ammon to fight against them': the enemy nation.

readings.first: 'the children of Ammon were subdued before the children of Israel': the nation defeated.
readings.second: 'Thus the children of Ammon were subdued before the children of Israel': a defeated nation.

readings.first: 'the children of Ammon were subdued before the children of Israel': the nation in war.
readings.second: 'the children of Ammon were subdued before the children of Israel': one nation defeated before another.

readings.first: 'taken vengeance for thee of thine enemies, even of the children of Ammon': the nation as enemy.
readings.second: 'taken vengeance for thee of thine enemies, even of the children of Ammon': the enemy nation.

readings.first: 'Wherefore passedst thou over to fight against the children of Ammon': the nation as the enemy fought.
readings.second: 'Wherefore passedst thou over to fight against the children of Ammon': the enemy nation.

readings.first: 'I and my people were at great strife with the children of Ammon': the nation as adversary.
readings.second: 'I and my people were at great strife with the children of Ammon': the enemy nation.

readings.first: 'passed over against the children of Ammon, and the LORD delivered them into my hand': the nation, then 'them'.
readings.second: 'passed over against the children of Ammon, and the LORD delivered them into my hand': the enemy nation.

readings.first: 'And she fastened it with the pin, and said unto him' carries on from 16:13, where Delilah spoke to Samson; only the feminine verb form stands for her.
readings.second: 'she fastened it with the pin, and said unto him' continues 'Delilah said unto Samson' of 16:13; the Hebrew has only the feminine verbs.

readings.first: 'Now the children of Benjamin heard that the children of Israel were gone up to Mizpeh': the tribe hears and acts.
readings.second: 'the children of Benjamin heard that the children of Israel were gone up to Mizpeh': the tribe as a body.

readings.first: 'her mother in law saw what she had gleaned' is Ruth's mother-in-law, called Naomi in 2:20: 'Naomi said unto her daughter in law'.
readings.second: Ruth's 'mother in law' is Naomi, as 2:20 'And Naomi said unto her daughter in law' confirms right after.

readings.first: 'Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly' at Gilgal: the nation as a body.
readings.second: 'Saul and all the men of Israel rejoiced greatly' at Gilgal, where 'all the people' made Saul king.

readings.first: 'all the men of Israel which had hid themselves in mount Ephraim' followed the fleeing Philistines: the nation's men.
readings.second: 'all the men of Israel which had hid themselves in mount Ephraim ... followed hard after them': the nation's fighting men.

readings.first: 'fought against all his enemies... against Moab, and against the children of Ammon': the nation as one of Saul's enemies.
readings.second: 'fought against all his enemies ... against Moab, and against the children of Ammon, and against Edom': a nation among Saul's enemies.

readings.first: 'am not I a Philistine' is said by the champion who 'stood and cried' to Israel; 17:10 calls the speaker 'the Philistine' and 17:4 names the champion Goliath.
readings.second: The champion named Goliath in 17:4 stands and says 'am not I a Philistine', in Hebrew 'the Philistine' with the pronoun 'I' (word 18).

readings.first: 'the Philistine said, I defy the armies of Israel' is the champion of Gath named Goliath in 17:4, who speaks the same challenge in 17:23.
readings.second: 'the Philistine said, I defy the armies of Israel' is the champion of 17:4, 'named Goliath, of Gath', still speaking.

readings.first: 'those words of the Philistine' are the challenge of 17:8-10 spoken by the champion named Goliath in 17:4.
readings.second: 'those words of the Philistine' are the challenge of 17:8-10 spoken by the champion 'named Goliath' of 17:4.

readings.first: 'the Philistine drew near morning and evening, and presented himself forty days' is the champion of 17:4 and 17:10, whose challenge Israel heard.
readings.second: 'the Philistine drew near morning and evening' is the challenger of 17:4-10, whom 17:23 calls 'the Philistine of Gath, Goliath by name'.

readings.first: 'he drew near to the Philistine' is David going to meet the champion of 17:4, who came against him in 17:41.
readings.second: 'he drew near to the Philistine' is David going to the champion whom 17:23 calls 'the Philistine of Gath, Goliath by name'.

readings.first: 'the Philistine came on and drew near unto David' is the champion of 17:4; 17:48 then has David run to meet 'the Philistine'.
readings.second: 'the Philistine came on and drew near unto David' with his shield-bearer (17:7) is the champion 'Goliath by name' of 17:23.

readings.first: 'the Philistine looked about, and saw David, he disdained him' is the champion who approached David in 17:41.
readings.second: 'the Philistine looked about, and saw David' is the champion David went out against, 'Goliath by name' in 17:23.

readings.first: 'the Philistine said unto David, Am I a dog' is the champion of 17:4, who meets David in 17:41-42.
readings.second: 'the Philistine said unto David, Am I a dog' is the champion David went out against, 'Goliath by name' in 17:23; words 19-20 say it again.

readings.first: 'the Philistine said to David, Come to me' is the champion of 17:4 who meets David; David answers him in 17:45.
readings.second: 'the Philistine said to David, Come to me' is the champion David went out against, 'Goliath by name' in 17:23.

readings.first: 'Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword' answers the champion who cursed David in 17:43-44.
readings.second: 'Then said David to the Philistine, Thou comest to me with a sword' addresses the champion 'Goliath by name' of 17:23.

readings.first: 'smote the Philistine in his forehead' is the champion who 'arose, and came' toward David in 17:48.
readings.second: 'smote the Philistine in his forehead' is the champion of 17:23, and 21:9 says 'Goliath the Philistine, whom thou slewest in the valley of Elah'.

readings.first: 'David prevailed over the Philistine... and smote the Philistine, and slew him' is the champion of 17:48-49 whose sword is in 21:9 called 'Goliath the Philistine'.
readings.second: 'David prevailed over the Philistine ... and slew him' is the one 21:9 names 'Goliath the Philistine, whom thou slewest'; words 17-18 say it again.

readings.first: 'stood upon the Philistine, and took his sword... slew him' is the champion struck down in 17:49-50; the Philistines then 'saw their champion was dead'.
readings.second: 'stood upon the Philistine, and took his sword ... and slew him' is the one 21:9 names 'Goliath the Philistine, whom thou slewest', also 'their champion' here.

readings.first: 'David took the head of the Philistine' is the head of the champion slain in 17:50-51.
readings.second: 'David took the head of the Philistine' he had just slain, whom 17:23 and 21:9 name Goliath.

readings.first: 'David go forth against the Philistine' is David going out to the champion who defied Israel in 17:10.
readings.second: 'Saul saw David go forth against the Philistine' is the champion of the chapter, 'the Philistine of Gath, Goliath by name' in 17:23.

readings.first: 'the slaughter of the Philistine' and 'the head of the Philistine' refer to the champion David killed in 17:50-51.
readings.second: 'David returned from the slaughter of the Philistine ... with the head of the Philistine in his hand' is the slain champion, Goliath in 17:23 and 21:9.

readings.first: 'David was returned from the slaughter of the Philistine' is the champion he killed in 17:50-51 and whose head he took in 17:54.
readings.second: 'when David was returned from the slaughter of the Philistine' repeats 17:57 and means the one 21:9 names 'Goliath the Philistine, whom thou slewest'.

readings.first: 'Ishbosheth said to Abner, Wherefore hast thou gone in unto my father's concubine?' and 3:8 'the words of Ishbosheth'; the Hebrew has only the verb 'and he said'.
readings.second: The Hebrew has only 'and he said to Abner' with no name; 3:8 'the words of Ishbosheth' and 'my father's concubine' (Saul's) show the speaker is Ishbosheth, as the King James supplies.

readings.first: 'Saul's son' who heard Abner was dead is Ishbosheth: 4:5 calls the house of the same captains' master 'the house of Ishbosheth' and 4:8 'Ishbosheth the son of Saul'.
readings.second: 'Saul's son' whose captains are Baanah and Rechab (4:2) is the man they kill in 4:5-8, 'Ishbosheth the son of Saul'.

readings.first: 'Of Syria, and of Moab, and of the children of Ammon': spoil dedicated from the nation, listed with other nations.
readings.second: 'of Syria, and of Moab, and of the children of Ammon': one of the 'nations which he subdued' (v.11).

readings.first: 'the children of Ammon saw that they stank before David, the children of Ammon sent and hired the Syrians': the nation acts.
readings.second: 'the children of Ammon saw that they stank before David, the children of Ammon sent and hired the Syrians': the nation acting in war.

readings.first: 'the children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array': the nation as an army.
readings.second: 'the children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array at the entering in of the gate': the nation's army.

readings.first: 'put them in array against the children of Ammon': the Ammonite army as the enemy.
readings.second: 'put them in array against the children of Ammon': the enemy army of the nation.

readings.first: 'if the children of Ammon be too strong for thee': the Ammonite force.
readings.second: 'if the children of Ammon be too strong for thee': the enemy army, set beside the Syrians.

readings.first: 'the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians were fled, then fled they also' and 'Joab returned from the children of Ammon': the nation's army.
readings.second: 'the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians were fled, then fled they also ... Joab returned from the children of Ammon': the nation's army in battle.

readings.first: 'the Syrians feared to help the children of Ammon any more': the nation as those the Syrians had helped.
readings.second: 'the Syrians feared to help the children of Ammon any more': the nation at war with Israel.

readings.first: 'they destroyed the children of Ammon, and besieged Rabbah': Joab and Israel destroy the nation.
readings.second: 'they destroyed the children of Ammon, and besieged Rabbah': the nation attacked by Israel.

readings.first: 'slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon': the Ammonite nation as the ones whose sword killed Uriah.
readings.second: 'slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon': the enemy nation in whose battle Uriah fell.

readings.first: 'Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon': the city belonging to the Ammonite nation.
readings.second: 'fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city': the city is named as the people's royal city.

readings.first: 'all the cities of the children of Ammon': the cities of the Ammonite nation, where David did this to the people in them.
readings.second: 'thus did he unto all the cities of the children of Ammon': the nation's cities and 'the people that were therein'.

readings.first: 'Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon': Rabbah named as the Ammonites' city.
readings.second: 'Shobi the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the children of Ammon': Rabbah is named as the people's city, the nation as a body.

readings.first: 'Ittai the son of Ribai out of Gibeah of the children of Benjamin': the town named as belonging to the Benjamite tribe.
readings.second: 'Ittai the son of Ribai out of Gibeah of the children of Benjamin': the town is named as belonging to the tribe.

readings.first: 'when all Israel saw that the king hearkened not... to your tents, O Israel... So Israel departed unto their tents': the nation as a body.
readings.second: 'when all Israel saw ... to your tents, O Israel ... So Israel departed unto their tents': the (northern) tribes as a body rejecting Rehoboam.

readings.first: 'he assembled all the house of Judah, with the tribe of Benjamin, an hundred and fourscore thousand chosen men': the tribe as a fighting body.
readings.second: 'all the house of Judah, with the tribe of Benjamin, an hundred and fourscore thousand chosen men': the tribe's warriors.

readings.first: Rehoboam assembled Judah and Benjamin 'to fight against the house of Israel': the northern nation as a body.
readings.second: 'to fight against the house of Israel': the tribes that made Jeroboam king (12:20), a body of the people set against Judah and Benjamin.

readings.first: 'made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi': the tribe of Levi, from which priests were properly taken.
readings.second: 'made priests of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi': the tribe, centuries after Levi.

readings.first: 'And he sent messengers to Ahab' continues from 20:1, where Benhadad the king of Syria gathered his host and besieged Samaria; the subject is only the verb's person.
readings.second: 'he sent messengers to Ahab' continues 'Benhadad the king of Syria' of 20:1; the Hebrew verse holds only the verb, the King James 'Thus saith Benhadad' standing in Hebrew 20:3.

readings.first: 'the king of Israel' answering Benhadad's messengers is Ahab, named in the same scene as 'Ahab king of Israel' (1KI 20:13) and 'Ahab' (20:34).
readings.second: 'the king of Israel' who answers Benhadad is named two verses on: 'a prophet unto Ahab king of Israel' (20:13), as already in 20:2.

readings.first: 'the king of Israel' to whom the man of God speaks is Ahab, the king of Israel of the same war (1KI 20:13, 20:34, 20:40).
readings.second: 'the king of Israel' fighting Benhadad in this chapter is 'Ahab king of Israel' of 20:13 and 'Ahab said' of 20:14.

readings.first: 'go out to the king of Israel' is the king whom Benhadad's servants approach and who is called 'Ahab' in 1KI 20:34, the same scene.
readings.second: Benhadad's servants will 'go out to the king of Israel', the victor of this war, named 'Ahab king of Israel' in 20:13.

readings.first: 'came to the king of Israel' is the king who answers 'he is my brother' and is named 'Ahab' two verses on (1KI 20:34).
readings.second: They 'came to the king of Israel', who calls Benhadad 'my brother'; the chapter names this king 'Ahab king of Israel' in 20:13-14.

readings.first: 'the king of Israel went to his house... and came to Samaria' is the king of Israel of 20:41; 21:1 names 'Ahab king of Samaria' at once after.
readings.second: 'the king of Israel went to his house ... to Samaria' is the king of this chapter, 'Ahab king of Israel' (20:13), 'Ahab king of Samaria' in the next verse 21:1.

readings.first: 'the king of Israel' visited by Jehoshaphat is the king who plans Ramothgilead; 1KI 22:20 asks 'Who shall persuade Ahab... at Ramothgilead?', and 21:29 sets Ahab's days here.
readings.second: 'the king of Israel' whom Jehoshaphat visits and who goes to Ramothgilead is named in 22:20, 'Who shall persuade Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramothgilead'.

readings.first: 'the king of Israel' who speaks of Ramoth in Gilead is the one 1KI 22:20 names as Ahab going up to Ramothgilead.
readings.second: 'the king of Israel' who plans to take Ramoth in Gilead is Ahab, named in 22:20 'Who shall persuade Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramothgilead'.

readings.first: 'the king of Syria' holding Ramoth in Gilead is not named in 22:1-5; the text does not say he is the Benhadad of chapter 20.
readings.second: 'the king of Syria' holding Ramoth is unnamed here, but 22:1 counts 'three years without war' from the covenant with Benhadad king of Syria in 20:34.
readings.settled: Kept: 1 Kings 22:1 counts the three years without war from the covenant with Benhadad king of Syria in 20:34, and the book names no other king of Syria until Hazael (2KI 8:15); the record is Benhadad king of Aram from 1KI 15 on.

readings.first: 'the king of Israel' with whom Jehoshaphat allies for Ramothgilead is Ahab, per 1KI 22:20 ('persuade Ahab... at Ramothgilead').
readings.second: 'Jehoshaphat said to the king of Israel' answers the king who asks him to Ramothgilead, named Ahab in 22:20; the opening 'he said' is the same king.

readings.first: 'the king of Israel' told to enquire of the LORD is the Ramothgilead king that 1KI 22:20 names Ahab.
readings.second: 'Jehoshaphat said unto the king of Israel' addresses the king going against Ramothgilead, whom 22:20 names: 'Who shall persuade Ahab'.

readings.first: 'the king of Israel gathered the prophets... Shall I go against Ramothgilead' is the king 1KI 22:20 calls Ahab, going up to Ramothgilead.
readings.second: 'the king of Israel gathered the prophets' to ask about Ramothgilead; 22:20 names him, 'Who shall persuade Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramothgilead'.

readings.first: 'the king of Israel' who hates Micaiah is the king of the Ramothgilead campaign that 1KI 22:20 names Ahab.
readings.second: 'the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat' of Micaiah 'I hate him'; Micaiah's vision in 22:20 names this king Ahab.

readings.first: 'the king of Israel called an officer' for Micaiah is the same Ahab of the Ramothgilead campaign (1KI 22:20).
readings.second: 'the king of Israel called an officer' to fetch Micaiah, whose vision in 22:20 names the king: 'Who shall persuade Ahab'.

readings.first: 'the king of Israel' sitting with Jehoshaphat at the gate of Samaria is the king of the Ramothgilead episode, Ahab (1KI 22:20).
readings.second: 'the king of Israel' sitting with Jehoshaphat at the gate of Samaria is the king of this account, named Ahab in 22:20.

readings.first: 'the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat, Did I not tell thee' is the Micaiah-scene king, Ahab (1KI 22:20).
readings.second: 'the king of Israel said unto Jehoshaphat' about Micaiah's prophecy, and two verses on the vision names him: 'Who shall persuade Ahab' (22:20).

readings.first: 'And he said, Hear thou the word of the LORD' continues Micaiah's answer to the king, who is named Micaiah in 22:15 and complains in 22:18 that 'he would prophesy no good concerning me'.
readings.second: 'And he said ... I saw the LORD' continues the speech of the prophet the king asked in 22:15 'Micaiah, shall we go'; Hebrew has only the verb, no pronoun word.

readings.first: 'the king of Syria commanded his thirty and two captains' is not named in this scene; the text does not tie him to Benhadad of chapter 20.
readings.second: 'the king of Syria' with 'his thirty and two captains' is unnamed here, but 22:1 continues the war with Benhadad of 20:1 and 20:34, who had thirty and two kings replaced by captains (20:24).
readings.settled: Kept: the king of Syria of 22:31 is the one of 22:1-3 whose war with Israel continues from Benhadad's covenant in 20:34; his thirty and two captains answer the thirty and two kings of 20:1, 20:24.

readings.first: 'the king of Israel' the Syrian captains seek (22:31) is Ahab of this battle, though they wrongly take Jehoshaphat for him; Ahab is named in 22:20.
readings.second: The captains, told to fight 'only with the king of Israel' (22:31), say 'Surely it is the king of Israel': the title means Ahab, though they wrongly apply it to Jehoshaphat (22:33).

readings.first: 'So he died according to the word of the LORD which Elijah had spoken... he had no son' is the sick king of 1:2-16, whose acts are called 'the acts of Ahaziah' in 1:18.
readings.second: 'So he died according to the word of the LORD which Elijah had spoken' is the king told 'shalt surely die' in 1:16, Ahaziah of 1:2 and 1:18; only the verb carries him.

readings.first: 'the king of Moab' is the Mesha of 2KI 3:4, 'Mesha king of Moab', the king Israel, Judah and Edom fought in this same chapter (3:5, 3:7).
readings.second: 'the king of Moab' in this campaign is Mesha: 3:4 'Mesha king of Moab', 3:5 'the king of Moab rebelled', and the war of 3:7 is against him.

readings.first: 'as the king of Israel was passing by upon the wall' (6:26) in the siege of Samaria names no king, so the text leaves open who he is.
readings.second: 'the king of Israel' on the wall is unnamed; the siege falls in the reign of 'Jehoram the son of Ahab' (3:1, 8:16), and 6:32 calls this king 'this son of a murderer'.
readings.settled: Kept: the king on the wall of besieged Samaria is 'this son of a murderer' (6:32), a son of Ahab, and of Ahab's sons Ahaziah died without a son (1:17) and Jehoram reigned in Samaria (3:1).

readings.first: 'the king of Israel hath hired against us the kings of the Hittites' (7:6) is the Syrians' phrase for an unnamed king; Jehoram is not named or identified here.
readings.second: The Syrians' 'the king of Israel hath hired against us' means the king besieged in Samaria, unnamed but within the reign of 'Jehoram the son of Ahab' (3:1, 8:16).
readings.settled: Kept: the king the Syrians fear in 7:6 is the king besieged in Samaria, 'this son of a murderer' of 6:32, Ahab's son Jehoram (3:1).

readings.first: 'as the man of God had said' points back to 7:1-2, where Elisha speaks to the king and the lord answers 'the man of God'.
readings.second: 'the man of God ... who spake when the king came down to him' is Elisha, who speaks in 7:1 when the king comes to him (6:32-33).

readings.first: 'the man of God had spoken to the king' repeats the words of Elisha in 7:1, answered in 7:2 by the lord addressing 'the man of God'.
readings.second: 'the man of God had spoken to the king' the word about the measures for a shekel, which 7:1 gives as 'Then Elisha said'.

readings.first: 'that lord answered the man of God' retells 7:2, where Elisha's word of 7:1 is answered by the lord addressing 'the man of God'.
readings.second: 'that lord answered the man of God' repeats 7:2, where the lord answers the Elisha who spoke in 7:1.

readings.first: 'the king of Syria oppressed them' in Jehoahaz's days is Hazael king of Syria, of whom 13:22 says 'Hazael king of Syria oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz'.
readings.second: 'the king of Syria oppressed them' in Jehoahaz's day is said by name in 13:22, 'Hazael king of Syria oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz'.

readings.first: 'the king of Syria had destroyed them' of Jehoahaz's people is Hazael, who by 13:22 'oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz'.
readings.second: 'the king of Syria had destroyed them' is said of Jehoahaz's people, and 13:22 has 'Hazael king of Syria oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz'.

readings.first: 'the king of Israel, which rise up against me' is the Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel who came up with Rezin against Jerusalem in 16:5.
readings.second: The kings who 'rise up against me' are those of 16:5, 'Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel'.

readings.first: Ahaz sent a present 'to the king of Assyria', the king he had just appealed to in 16:7 as 'Tiglathpileser king of Assyria'.
readings.second: Ahaz 'sent it for a present to the king of Assyria', the Tiglathpileser king of Assyria to whom he sent messengers in 16:7.

readings.first: 'the king of Assyria did carry away Israel' follows 18:9-10 where 'Shalmaneser king of Assyria' besieged and took Samaria; the same king carries Israel away.
readings.second: After 'Shalmaneser king of Assyria came up against Samaria' (18:9) and its fall (18:10), 'the king of Assyria did carry away Israel' continues with the same king.

readings.words: the king of Assyria his master
readings.first: 'the king of Assyria his master hath sent' Rabshakeh is Sennacherib king of Assyria, who sent him (18:13, 18:17) and whose words are named in 19:16.
readings.second: Rabshakeh was sent by 'the king of Assyria his master'; 19:16 says 'hear the words of Sennacherib, which hath sent him to reproach the living God'.

readings.first: 'the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me' speak of Sennacherib, whose messenger Rabshakeh the verse before names as sent by 'the king of Assyria his master' (19:4, 19:16).
readings.second: 'the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me' refers to the sender of Rabshakeh, named in 19:16 and 19:20 as 'Sennacherib king of Assyria'.

readings.first: 'Rabshakeh... found the king of Assyria warring against Libnah' is Sennacherib, the king of Assyria whose messenger he was in this account (19:4, 19:16).
readings.second: Rabshakeh 'found the king of Assyria warring against Libnah', the king who had come against Judah's cities in 18:13, 'Sennacherib king of Assyria'.

readings.first: 'the hand of the king of Assyria' is the king whose envoys speak to Hezekiah, Sennacherib (18:13, 19:16, 19:36).
readings.second: The message says Jerusalem will be given 'into the hand of the king of Assyria', i.e. the sender himself, whose letter Hezekiah spreads before the LORD as 'the words of Sennacherib' (19:16).

readings.first: 'the remnant that is escaped of the house of Judah shall yet again take root downward': the people's survivors.
readings.second: 'the remnant that is escaped of the house of Judah shall yet again take root': the nation's survivors.

readings.first: 'the LORD concerning the king of Assyria, He shall not come into this city' is about Sennacherib, for whom Hezekiah prayed in 19:20 and who departed in 19:36.
readings.second: The oracle 'concerning the king of Assyria' answers Hezekiah's prayer 'against Sennacherib king of Assyria' (19:20); 19:36 'So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed'.

readings.first: 'deliver thee and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria' is the Assyrian king threatening Hezekiah's Jerusalem in this time, Sennacherib (18:13, 19:36).
readings.second: 'deliver thee and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria ... for my servant David's sake' repeats the promise of 19:34 against Sennacherib, named in 19:20 and 19:36.

readings.first: 'the book which the king of Judah hath read': the king of Judah is king Josiah, who sent Shaphan to the house of the LORD (22:1-3).
readings.second: 'the book which the king of Judah hath read' is the book Shaphan read before king Josiah (22:3, 22:10), who sent to Huldah.

readings.first: 'the king of Judah which sent you to enquire of the LORD' is the king Josiah who sent Shaphan and the others (22:3, 22:12-14).
readings.second: 'the king of Judah which sent you to enquire of the LORD' is Josiah, who sent Hilkiah and the others to Huldah (22:3, 22:12-14).

readings.first: 'the king of Babylon had taken from the river of Egypt' is the king of Babylon of 24:1, 'Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon', in the days of Jehoiakim.
readings.second: In Jehoiakim's days 'Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up' (24:1); 'the king of Babylon had taken from the river of Egypt' is that same king.

readings.first: Nebuzaradan brought them 'to the king of Babylon to Riblah'; 25:8 and 25:22 name him as 'Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon'.
readings.second: Nebuzaradan brought them 'to the king of Babylon to Riblah'; 25:8 dates this to 'king Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon' and 25:22 names him again.

readings.first: 'Mizraim begat Ludim': the son of Mizraim in the list, Lud under the plural form Ludim.
readings.second: 'Mizraim begat Ludim' repeats GEN 10:13, the text for this son of Mizraim; Ludim is the plural (people) form of the name Lud.

readings.words: the daughter of Shua the Canaanitess
readings.first: 'born unto him of the daughter of Shua the Canaanitess' is the mother of Er, Onan and Shelah; the record itself is defined by this verse.
readings.second: The Hebrew words 'bath Shua' (12-13), printed 'the daughter of Shua the Canaanitess', are the record's own name, the mother of Er, Onan and Shelah.

readings.first: The verse lists 'the sons of Elioenai were, Hodaiah', and word 4 is the Hebrew Hodaviah; the same name printed in another spelling.
readings.second: The name itself is printed: 'the sons of Elioenai were, Hodaiah', the Hebrew word 4 being Hodaviah as written.

readings.first: 'some of them, even of the sons of Simeon, five hundred men, went to mount Seir': a body of men of the tribe on a campaign.
readings.second: 'some of them, even of the sons of Simeon, five hundred men, went to mount Seir' in Hezekiah's days: tribesmen, not Simeon's own sons.

readings.first: 'the children of Gad dwelt over against them, in the land of Bashan unto Salcah': the tribe settled in Bashan.
readings.second: 'the children of Gad dwelt over against them, in the land of Bashan unto Salcah': the tribe's settlement.

readings.first: 'The sons of Reuben, and the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh, of valiant men... went out to the war': the tribal half's army.
readings.second: 'The sons of Reuben, and the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh, of valiant men... four and forty thousand': the tribe's army.

readings.first: 'The sons of Reuben, and the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh, of valiant men... that went out to the war': a tribal army.
readings.second: 'The sons of Reuben, and the Gadites... four and forty thousand... that went out to the war': the tribe's fighting men.

readings.words: the children of the half tribe of Manasseh
readings.first: 'the children of the half tribe of Manasseh dwelt in the land: they increased': the tribal half as dwellers who multiplied.
readings.second: 'the children of the half tribe of Manasseh dwelt in the land: they increased from Bashan unto Baalhermon'.

readings.first: 'the firstborn Vashni' names another firstborn, while 1 Samuel 8:2 gives Joel as firstborn; the text does not say whether Vashni is Joel under another name.
readings.second: 'the sons of Samuel; the firstborn Vashni, and Abiah': 1CH 6:33 names Samuel's son Joel and 1SA 8:2 'his firstborn was Joel... his second, Abiah', so the firstborn here is Joel under another form.
readings.settled: Kept, of the verse only: the firstborn of Samuel is Joel in the same chapter, 'Joel, the son of Shemuel' (1CH 6:33); the word printed Vashni is not given to him.

readings.first: 'out of the tribe of Benjamin; Geba... Alemeth... Anathoth': the tribe gives cities to the Levites.
readings.second: 'out of the tribe of Benjamin; Geba with her suburbs': cities given out of the tribe's inheritance.

readings.words: the sons of Kohath, which were left of the family of that tribe
readings.first: 'unto the sons of Kohath, which were left... were cities given': the clan as recipients of cities.
readings.second: 'unto the sons of Kohath, which were left of the family of that tribe, were cities given... ten cities': the clan's allotment.

readings.first: 'to the sons of Gershom throughout their families out of the tribe of Issachar... thirteen cities': same allotment as Joshua 21:6 'the children of Gershon'; 1 Chr 6:1 lists Gershom as Levi's son.
readings.second: 'to the sons of Gershom throughout their families... thirteen cities': the Levite clan; Chronicles spells Levi's son Gershom (1Ch 6:16), parallel to 'children of Gershon' in Jos 21:6.

readings.first: 'to the sons of Gershom... out of the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities': the tribe as giver of cities.
readings.second: 'out of the tribe of Manasseh in Bashan, thirteen cities': cities given to the Gershomites from the tribe's inheritance.

readings.first: 'out of the tribe of Reuben, and out of the tribe of Gad, and out of the tribe of Zebulun, twelve cities': the tribe giving cities to Merari.
readings.second: 'Unto the sons of Merari were given by lot... out of the tribe of Gad': Levitical cities from the tribe's lot.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Benjamin
readings.first: 'they gave by lot out of... the tribe of the children of Benjamin, these cities': the tribe gives cities.
readings.second: 'out of the tribe of the children of Benjamin, these cities': cities given from the tribe.

readings.words: the tribe of the children of Simeon
readings.first: 'out of the tribe of the children of Simeon... these cities, which are called by their names': the tribe gives Levite cities.
readings.second: 'they gave by lot... out of the tribe of the children of Simeon... these cities': the tribe giving Levitical cities.

readings.words: the residue of the families of the sons of Kohath
readings.first: 'the residue of the families of the sons of Kohath had cities of their coasts out of the tribe of Ephraim': a clan with families.
readings.second: 'the residue of the families of the sons of Kohath had cities of their coasts out of the tribe of Ephraim': the clan.

readings.words: the family of the remnant of the sons of Kohath
readings.first: 'for the family of the remnant of the sons of Kohath': the clan receives cities.
readings.second: 'Aner... and Bileam... for the family of the remnant of the sons of Kohath': cities given to the clan.

readings.first: 'out of the half tribe of Manasseh; Aner with her suburbs, and Bileam': the tribal half gives cities to Kohath's remnant.
readings.second: 'out of the half tribe of Manasseh; Aner with her suburbs, and Bileam': cities from the tribe's inheritance for Kohath.

readings.first: 'Unto the sons of Gershom were given out of the family of the half tribe of Manasseh, Golan in Bashan': the clan given cities, as in Joshua 21:27 'children of Gershon'.
readings.second: 'Unto the sons of Gershom were given... Golan in Bashan': the Levite clan (Gershom for Gershon as in 1Ch 6:16), parallel to Jos 21:27.

readings.words: the family of the half tribe of Manasseh
readings.first: 'Unto the sons of Gershom were given out of the family of the half tribe of Manasseh, Golan in Bashan': the tribal half as giver of cities.
readings.second: 'Unto the sons of Gershom were given out of the family of the half tribe of Manasseh, Golan in Bashan'.
