readings.first: 'out of the tribe of Gad; Ramoth in Gilead with her suburbs, and Mahanaim': cities from the tribe's holding; the tribe is what is named.
readings.second: 'out of the tribe of Gad; Ramoth in Gilead with her suburbs, and Mahanaim': cities from the tribe's possession.

readings.first: 'by the borders of the children of Manasseh, Bethshean and her towns... In these dwelt the children of Joseph': towns held by the tribe, the tribe named as owner.
readings.second: 'by the borders of the children of Manasseh, Bethshean and her towns... In these dwelt the children of Joseph': the tribe's holdings.

readings.first: 'All these were the children of Asher, heads of their father's house... number... twenty and six thousand men': the tribe's heads and its mustered men.
readings.second: 'All these were the children of Asher ... apt to the war ... twenty and six thousand men': the tribe's descendants reckoned as a body.

readings.first: 'the son of Jonathan was Meribbaal; and Meribbaal begat Micah': Jonathan's son with a son Micah matches Mephibosheth, whose young son was Micha (2 Samuel 9:12); the verse does not itself say so.
readings.second: 'the son of Jonathan was Meribbaal; and Meribbaal begat Micah' matches Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, who 'had a young son, whose name was Micha' (2SA 9:12), retold here.
readings.settled: Kept: Jonathan's son whose son is Micah is the Mephibosheth who 'had a young son, whose name was Micha' (2SA 9:12); the genealogy of Saul's house retells it, and Meribbaal is his name here.

readings.first: 'All these are of the sons of Benjamin': after listing Ulam's sons as persons, the verse counts them as belonging to the Benjamite tribe.
readings.second: 'All these are of the sons of Benjamin': the preceding generations counted as belonging to the tribe, not Benjamin's own sons.

readings.first: 'in Jerusalem dwelt of the children of Judah, and of the children of Benjamin, and of the children of Ephraim': the tribe's members dwelling there.
readings.second: 'in Jerusalem dwelt of the children of Judah, and of the children of Benjamin': members of the tribe as settlers.

readings.first: 'in Jerusalem dwelt of the children of Judah, and of the children of Benjamin, and of the children of Ephraim, and Manasseh': tribal members dwelling.
readings.second: 'in Jerusalem dwelt of the children of Judah... and of the children of Ephraim, and Manasseh': members of the tribe living in Jerusalem.

readings.first: 'And of the sons of Benjamin; Sallu the son of Meshullam': members of the tribe listed as dwellers in Jerusalem.
readings.second: 'of the sons of Benjamin; Sallu the son of Meshullam': a later member of the tribe dwelling in Jerusalem, not Benjamin's own son.

readings.first: 'they were porters in the companies of the children of Levi': the tribe's camps or divisions.
readings.second: 'they were porters in the companies of the children of Levi': the tribe's camps, in the days after the return.

readings.first: 'the son of Jonathan was Meribbaal: and Meribbaal begat Micah': Jonathan's son with a son Micah matches Mephibosheth, whose young son was Micha (2 Samuel 9:12); the verse does not itself say so.
readings.second: 'the son of Jonathan was Meribbaal: and Meribbaal begat Micah' matches Jonathan's son Mephibosheth, who 'had a young son, whose name was Micha' (2SA 9:12).
readings.settled: Kept: as 1 Chronicles 8:34, the list repeated.

readings.first: 'Ithai the son of Ribai of Gibeah, that pertained to the children of Benjamin': the town belongs to the Benjamite tribe.
readings.second: 'Gibeah, that pertained to the children of Benjamin': the town is named as belonging to the tribe.

readings.first: 'These were of the sons of Gad, captains of the host': Gadite warriors who joined David, a tribal body.
readings.second: 'These were of the sons of Gad, captains of the host': Gadite warriors in David's day, not Gad's own sons.

readings.first: 'there came of the children of Benjamin and Judah to the hold unto David': a body of men of the tribe, centuries after the ancestor.
readings.second: 'there came of the children of Benjamin and Judah to the hold unto David': men of the tribe joining David, long after Benjamin himself.

readings.first: 'Of the children of Simeon, mighty men of valour for the war, seven thousand and one hundred': the tribe's men at Hebron.
readings.second: 'Of the children of Simeon, mighty men of valour for the war, seven thousand and one hundred': the tribe's warriors coming to David.

readings.first: 'Of the children of Levi four thousand and six hundred': the tribe's warriors counted, like Judah and Simeon.
readings.second: 'Of the children of Levi four thousand and six hundred': the tribe's contingent coming to David, beside Judah and Simeon.

readings.first: 'of the children of Benjamin, the kindred of Saul, three thousand': a troop of the tribe coming to David.
readings.second: 'of the children of Benjamin, the kindred of Saul, three thousand': a tribal contingent counted among David's supporters.

readings.first: 'of the children of Ephraim twenty thousand and eight hundred, mighty men of valour': a tribal contingent coming to David.
readings.second: 'of the children of Ephraim twenty thousand and eight hundred, mighty men of valour': a tribal contingent coming to David.

readings.first: 'Elishama, and Beeliada, and Eliphalet' is the list of David's sons born in Jerusalem (14:4), which 2SA 5:16 and 1CH 3:8 give as Elishama, Eliada, Eliphelet.
readings.second: 'Beeliada' stands between Elishama and Eliphalet among David's sons born in Jerusalem, where the same list in 1CH 3:8 reads 'Elishama, and Eliada, and Eliphelet'.

readings.first: 'Of the sons of Kohath; Uriel the chief, and his brethren an hundred and twenty': the clan's delegation of Levites.
readings.second: 'Of the sons of Kohath; Uriel the chief, and his brethren an hundred and twenty': the clan in David's day, beside Merari and Gershom.

readings.first: 'Of the sons of Gershom; Joel the chief and his brethren an hundred and thirty': the Levite clan's group, beside Kohath and Merari; 'Gershom' spelled for Gershon's line.
readings.second: 'Of the sons of Gershom; Joel the chief and his brethren an hundred and thirty': the Levitical clan beside Kohath and Merari.

readings.first: 'O ye seed of Israel his servant, ye children of Jacob, his chosen ones': the descendants are addressed as a body, in parallel with 'children of Jacob'.
readings.second: 'O ye seed of Israel his servant, ye children of Jacob, his chosen ones': the descendants addressed as a body; Israel and Jacob name them through their ancestor.

readings.first: 'The LORD of hosts is the God of Israel, even a God to Israel'; verse 22 has 'thy people Israel': the nation.
readings.second: 'The LORD of hosts is the God of Israel, even a God to Israel': the people of 17:22, 'thy people Israel ... becamest their God'.

readings.first: 'the children of Ammon gathered themselves together from their cities, and came to battle': the nation gathers for war.
readings.second: 'the children of Ammon gathered themselves together from their cities, and came to battle': the nation mustering.

readings.first: 'the children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array': the nation as an army.
readings.second: 'the children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array before the gate': the nation's army.

readings.first: 'they set themselves in array against the children of Ammon': the Ammonite army as enemy.
readings.second: 'they set themselves in array against the children of Ammon': the enemy army.

readings.first: 'if the children of Ammon be too strong for thee': the Ammonite force.
readings.second: 'if the children of Ammon be too strong for thee': the enemy army beside the Syrians.

readings.first: 'the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians were fled, they likewise fled': the nation's army, then 'they'.
readings.second: 'when the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians were fled, they likewise fled': the nation's army.

readings.first: 'neither would the Syrians help the children of Ammon any more': the nation as those left without Syrian help.
readings.second: 'neither would the Syrians help the children of Ammon any more': the nation at war.

readings.first: 'wasted the country of the children of Ammon': the land named as the nation's own, which Joab laid waste.
readings.second: 'wasted the country of the children of Ammon, and came and besieged Rabbah': the land is named as the people's, in a war against them.

readings.first: 'all the cities of the children of Ammon': the cities of the Ammonite nation, whose people David brought out.
readings.second: 'Even so dealt David with all the cities of the children of Ammon': the nation's cities and their people.

readings.first: 'his sons were named of the tribe of Levi': Moses' sons are reckoned to the tribe, a body.
readings.second: 'his sons were named of the tribe of Levi': Moses' sons reckoned with the tribe rather than the priests.

readings.first: 'Of the sons of Izhar; Shelomith the chief': in a list of Levite houses, the sons of Izhar are a family body with a chief, not persons in a genealogy.
readings.second: 'Of the sons of Izhar; Shelomith the chief': a Levite family with its chief among David's divisions, not Izhar's own sons listed as persons.

readings.first: 'These were the sons of Levi after the house of their fathers... counted by number of names by their polls': the tribe's heads and workers, counted, not the man's own sons.
readings.second: 'These were the sons of Levi after the house of their fathers... that did the work for the service of the house of the LORD, from... twenty years'.

readings.words: the rest of the sons of Levi
readings.first: 'the rest of the sons of Levi were these': the remaining Levite families, then listed by descent from Amram.
readings.second: 'the rest of the sons of Levi were these: Of the sons of Amram; Shubael': later Levite houses under David, not Levi's own sons.

readings.first: 'The sons of Jehieli; Zetham, and Joel' is a Gershonite line like Jehiel of 23:8, but 23:8 makes Zetham and Joel his brothers, so whether Jehieli is Jehiel or a family is not settled.
readings.second: 'Jehieli' with 'Zetham, and Joel his brother' among the sons of Laadan (26:21) answers 23:8, 'The sons of Laadan; the chief was Jehiel, and Zetham, and Joel'; the form may be a clan name.
readings.settled: Kept, of the verse only: 'the sons of Jehieli; Zetham, and Joel his brother' among the sons of Laadan (26:21) answers 23:8, 'the sons of Laadan; the chief was Jehiel, and Zetham, and Joel'. The form is the family's, so no word is given to the man.

readings.first: 'Of the children of Perez was the chief of all the captains of the host for the first month': the Perez family of Judah supplies a captain.
readings.second: 'Of the children of Perez was the chief of all the captains of the host': Jashobeam (27:2) reckoned by his clan, not Perez himself.

readings.first: 'Helez the Pelonite, of the children of Ephraim': a captain belonging to the tribe.
readings.second: 'Helez the Pelonite, of the children of Ephraim': the captain's tribe.

readings.first: 'Benaiah the Pirathonite, of the children of Ephraim': a captain belonging to the tribe.
readings.second: 'Benaiah the Pirathonite, of the children of Ephraim': the captain's tribe.

readings.first: 'Of the children of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Azaziah' (prince of the tribes of Israel, 27:22): the tribe and its ruler.
readings.second: 'Of the children of Ephraim, Hoshea the son of Azaziah': the prince over the tribe among 'the princes of the tribes of Israel' (27:22).

readings.first: 'of the half tribe of Manasseh, Joel the son of Pedaiah... princes of the tribes of Israel': the tribal half's officer.
readings.second: 'of the half tribe of Manasseh, Joel the son of Pedaiah': a prince of the tribes of Israel under David (27:22).

readings.first: 'the children of Judah prevailed, because they relied upon the LORD God of their fathers': the army and people of Judah.
readings.second: 'the children of Judah prevailed, because they relied upon the LORD': the kingdom's army against Israel.

readings.first: 'Again he said, Therefore hear the word of the LORD' is Micaiah speaking, answering the king of Israel's complaint of 18:17 and following 'Micaiah said' in 18:13.
readings.second: 'Again he said ... I saw the LORD' continues Micaiah's answer (18:13 'And Micaiah said'); the speaker is only in the verb, no pronoun word.

readings.first: 'the children of Moab, and the children of Ammon... came against Jehoshaphat to battle': the nation as an invading body.
readings.second: 'the children of Moab, and the children of Ammon... came against Jehoshaphat to battle': the nation at war.

readings.first: 'the children of Ammon and Moab and mount Seir' are named as peoples who now come against Judah, spared by Israel at the exodus.
readings.second: 'the children of Ammon and Moab and mount Seir, whom thou wouldest not let Israel invade': nations coming against Judah.

readings.first: 'the LORD set ambushments against the children of Ammon, Moab, and mount Seir, which were come against Judah': the nation as invaders.
readings.second: 'the LORD set ambushments against the children of Ammon, Moab, and mount Seir, which were come against Judah': an invading army.

readings.first: 'the children of Ammon and Moab stood up against the inhabitants of mount Seir, utterly to slay and destroy them': the nation acting.
readings.second: 'the children of Ammon and Moab stood up against the inhabitants of mount Seir': the nation's army.

readings.first: 'the LORD is not with Israel, to wit, with all the children of Ephraim': the text itself equates this Israel with the children of Ephraim, the northern host hired by Amaziah.
readings.second: 'the LORD is not with Israel, to wit, with all the children of Ephraim': the Ephraimites as the northern body; the two 'Israel' words name the kingdom, not this record.

readings.first: The king's command 'Go, enquire of the LORD' (34:21, plural imperative) follows 34:20 'the king commanded Hilkiah, and Ahikam ... saying', so Hilkiah is among those addressed; only the verb's person marks him.
readings.second: The plural commands 'Go, enquire' are spoken to the men of 34:20, 'the king commanded Hilkiah, and Ahikam ...', so Hilkiah is addressed only through the verb's person, with four others.

readings.first: 'the book which they have read before the king of Judah': the king is Josiah (34:1), whom the king's messengers served in 34:22.
readings.second: 'the book which they have read before the king of Judah' is the book Shaphan read before Josiah (34:1, 34:18), whose envoys went to Huldah.

readings.first: 'as for the king of Judah, who sent you to enquire of the LORD' is the king who sent Hilkiah and the others (34:22); the king is Josiah (34:1).
readings.second: 'the king of Judah, who sent you to enquire of the LORD' is Josiah (34:1), whose men went to Huldah (34:20-22).

readings.first: The verse itself is the record's place: 'the last sons of Adonikam, whose names are these, Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah'; Jeiel is the same name as Jeuel spelled differently.
readings.second: 'of the last sons of Adonikam... Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah' is the very descendant of Adonikam going up with Ezra, spelled Jeiel here.

readings.first: 'the seed of Israel separated themselves from all strangers, and stood and confessed their sins': the returned community as a body.
readings.second: 'the seed of Israel separated themselves from all strangers, and stood and confessed their sins': the returned people as a body.

readings.first: 'Hodijah, Bani, Beninu' (10:13) names a Hodijah, but 10:10 has another and the text does not say whether they are two men or which one this record is.
readings.second: 'Hodijah' is printed in 10:13 as a second Levite of that name in the sealed list after the one of 10:10; the record is defined only by this list.
readings.settled: Kept: Hodijah is printed in NEH 10:13, and the record is the Hodijah of the sealed list at 10:13, as its line says.

readings.first: 'Hodijah' in 10:18 stands in the list headed 'The chief of the people' (10:14); the only Hodijah among the chiefs, so the non-Levite leader.
readings.second: 'Hodijah' is printed in the list headed 'The chief of the people' (10:14), so this is the non-Levite leader of that name.

readings.first: 'the children of Israel and the children of Levi shall bring the offering of the corn': the tribe as a body, with the priests, porters and singers.
readings.second: 'the children of Israel and the children of Levi shall bring the offering of the corn': the Levites of Nehemiah's covenant.

readings.first: 'at Jerusalem dwelt certain of the children of Judah, and of the children of Benjamin': members of the tribe settled in the city.
readings.second: 'at Jerusalem dwelt certain of the children of Judah, and of the children of Benjamin': members of the tribe settling Jerusalem after the exile.

readings.first: 'Athaiah the son of Uzziah... of the children of Perez': he belongs to the Perez clan living at Jerusalem.
readings.second: 'Athaiah... of the children of Perez': a clan of Judah dwelling at Jerusalem, counted in 11:6; 'Judah' (7, 14) is the wider tribe.

readings.first: 'All the sons of Perez that dwelt at Jerusalem were four hundred threescore and eight valiant men': the clan counted.
readings.second: 'All the sons of Perez that dwelt at Jerusalem were four hundred threescore and eight valiant men': the clan after the return.

readings.first: 'these are the sons of Benjamin; Sallu the son of Meshullam...': the Benjamite families dwelling in Jerusalem (11:4), listed by a descendant, not the man Benjamin's own sons.
readings.second: 'these are the sons of Benjamin; Sallu the son of Meshullam': post-exilic Benjamite residents of Jerusalem, not Benjamin's own sons.

readings.first: 'The children also of Benjamin from Geba dwelt at Michmash, and Aija, and Bethel': the tribe's members and where they lived.
readings.second: 'The children also of Benjamin from Geba dwelt at Michmash': the tribe's members settling towns after the exile.

readings.first: 'my soul... thine Holy One' are parallel terms for the speaker, and PSA 16:1 is headed 'Michtam of David'; the verse is read of the psalmist, not of a later figure.
readings.second: 'thine Holy One' stands parallel to 'my soul' of the speaker, whom the heading in 16:1 gives as 'Michtam of David'.

readings.first: 'all ye the seed of Jacob, glorify him; and fear him, all ye the seed of Israel': the descendants addressed as a body.
readings.second: 'all ye the seed of Jacob, glorify him; and fear him, all ye the seed of Israel': the descendants addressed as a body.

readings.first: 'our inheritance, the excellency of Jacob whom he loved': no name Israel is written; Jacob, loved and owning an inheritance, stands for the people, though the man could be meant.
readings.second: 'our inheritance for us, the excellency of Jacob whom he loved': Jacob stands for the 'us' of the psalm, the people given the land.
readings.settled: Kept: 'our inheritance ... the excellency of Jacob whom he loved' is the psalm's 'us' (47:3), the people given the land; Jacob stands for them.

readings.first: 'The children of Ephraim, being armed, and carrying bows, turned back in the day of battle': the tribe acting together.
readings.second: 'The children of Ephraim, being armed, and carrying bows, turned back in the day of battle': the tribe's army.

readings.first: 'O ye seed of Abraham his servant, ye children of Jacob his chosen': the descendants addressed; the name Israel is not written.
readings.second: 'O ye seed of Abraham his servant, ye children of Jacob his chosen': the descendants addressed as a body.

readings.first: 'he will bless the house of Israel; he will bless the house of Aaron': the nation as a body.
readings.second: 'he will bless the house of Israel; he will bless the house of Aaron': the nation beside its priestly house.

readings.first: 'Bless the LORD, O house of Israel: bless the LORD, O house of Aaron': the nation addressed.
readings.second: 'Bless the LORD, O house of Israel: bless the LORD, O house of Aaron': the nation called to worship.

readings.first: 'Bless the LORD, O house of Levi': the tribe addressed together with the houses of Israel and Aaron.
readings.second: 'Bless the LORD, O house of Levi': the tribe addressed beside the house of Israel and the house of Aaron.

readings.words: thy people the house of Jacob
readings.first: 'thou hast forsaken thy people the house of Jacob, because they be replenished from the east': the nation; the name Israel is not written.
readings.second: 'thou hast forsaken thy people the house of Jacob, because they be replenished from the east': the nation.

readings.first: 'the vineyard of the LORD of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant': the nation.
readings.second: 'the vineyard of the LORD of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah his pleasant plant': the nation as the vineyard.

readings.first: 'Rezin and Remaliah's son' is the pair of Isaiah 7:1-9, where 'Pekah the son of Remaliah' king of Israel and 'the head of Samaria is Remaliah's son' stand.
readings.second: 'Rezin and Remaliah's son' repeats the pair of 7:1, 'Rezin the king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel'.

readings.first: 'a stone of stumbling... to both the houses of Israel': the two houses of the nation.
readings.second: 'a rock of offence to both the houses of Israel': the people in its two kingdoms.

readings.first: 'the LORD, that hideth his face from the house of Jacob': the nation; the name Israel is not written in this verse.
readings.second: 'the LORD, that hideth his face from the house of Jacob': the nation.

readings.first: 'the remnant of Israel, and such as are escaped of the house of Jacob, shall no more stay upon him that smote them': the nation's survivors. 'Holy One of Israel' is God's title.
readings.second: 'the remnant of Israel, and such as are escaped of the house of Jacob ... the Holy One of Israel': the surviving nation and its God.

readings.first: 'the children of Ammon shall obey them': the nation subject to Israel, beside Edom and Moab.
readings.second: 'the children of Ammon shall obey them': a nation named with Edom, Moab and the Philistines.

readings.first: 'will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land': a people with a land, strangers joined to 'the house of Jacob'.
readings.second: 'mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land ... cleave to the house of Jacob': the nation restored.

readings.first: 'concerning the house of Jacob, Jacob shall not now be ashamed, neither shall his face wax pale': the nation; the name Israel is not written.
readings.second: 'concerning the house of Jacob, Jacob shall not now be ashamed': the nation personified, whose 'children' sanctify God (29:23).

readings.words: the great king, the king of Assyria
readings.first: Rabshakeh's 'the great king, the king of Assyria' is the king who sent him (36:2) and whom 36:1 and 37:21 name as Sennacherib king of Assyria.
readings.second: Rabshakeh speaks for 'the great king, the king of Assyria', the Sennacherib king of Assyria who came against Judah and sent him in 36:1-2.

readings.first: 'the hand of the king of Assyria' in Rabshakeh's speech is the same king who sent him (36:2), named Sennacherib in 36:1 and 37:21.
readings.second: In Rabshakeh's speech 'the king of Assyria' is his master Sennacherib, named king of Assyria in 36:1 as the one besieging Judah.

readings.first: 'thus saith the king of Assyria, Make an agreement with me' is Rabshakeh quoting his sender, the Sennacherib king of Assyria of 36:1-2.
readings.second: 'thus saith the king of Assyria' in Rabshakeh's message is Sennacherib, who sent Rabshakeh (36:1-2).

readings.first: 'out of the hand of the king of Assyria' in Rabshakeh's speech (36:13-20) is the king of Assyria Sennacherib of 36:1, who sent him.
readings.second: 'out of the hand of the king of Assyria' in Rabshakeh's speech means his master Sennacherib of 36:1-2.

readings.words: the king of Assyria his master
readings.first: 'the king of Assyria his master hath sent' Rabshakeh; Rabshakeh was sent by the king Sennacherib (36:1-2, 37:17).
readings.second: 'Rabshakeh, whom the king of Assyria his master hath sent to reproach the living God' is Sennacherib, as 37:17 says 'Sennacherib, which hath sent to reproach the living God'.

readings.first: 'the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me' refers to Rabshakeh's sender, Sennacherib king of Assyria (36:1-2, 37:17).
readings.second: 'the servants of the king of Assyria have blasphemed me' refers to Rabshakeh's master Sennacherib (36:1-2, 37:17).

readings.first: Rabshakeh 'found the king of Assyria warring against Libnah' is his own master, Sennacherib king of Assyria of this same episode (36:1-2, 37:17).
readings.second: Rabshakeh 'found the king of Assyria warring against Libnah', his master Sennacherib who had sent him from Lachish (36:1-2).

readings.first: 'the hand of the king of Assyria' in the message to Hezekiah is the same king of Assyria who is warring in 37:8 and is named Sennacherib in 37:17, 37:21.
readings.second: The messengers' letter says Jerusalem shall not be given 'into the hand of the king of Assyria', the sender Sennacherib (37:9, 37:17).

readings.words: the king of the city of Sepharvaim
readings.first: 'the king of the city of Sepharvaim' is the king of Sepharvaim of the same question in 2 Kings 19:13.
readings.second: 'the king of the city of Sepharvaim' is the same king named in 2KI 19:13, which this chapter retells, among kings the Assyrians destroyed.

readings.first: 'the remnant that is escaped of the house of Judah shall again take root downward': the people's survivors.
readings.second: 'the remnant that is escaped of the house of Judah shall again take root': the nation's survivors.

readings.first: 'thus saith the LORD concerning the king of Assyria' answers the prayer against 'Sennacherib king of Assyria' (37:21) and precedes 37:37 naming him.
readings.second: The oracle answering prayer 'against Sennacherib king of Assyria' (37:21) says 'concerning the king of Assyria, He shall not come into this city'.

readings.first: 'this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria' follows the siege of Jerusalem by Sennacherib king of Assyria in chapters 36-37; one step of reading ties it to him.
readings.second: 'deliver thee and this city out of the hand of the king of Assyria' promised to Hezekiah refers to the siege by Sennacherib king of Assyria of chapters 36-37 (37:37).

readings.words: thou worm Jacob, and ye men of Israel
readings.first: 'Fear not, thou worm Jacob, and ye men of Israel; I will help thee': the nation addressed. 'Holy One of Israel' is God's title.
readings.second: 'Fear not, thou worm Jacob, and ye men of Israel ... the Holy One of Israel': the nation addressed as a body.

readings.first: 'I said not unto the seed of Jacob, Seek ye me in vain': the descendants addressed as a body; the name Israel is not written in this verse.
readings.second: 'I said not unto the seed of Jacob, Seek ye me in vain': the descendants addressed as a body, the Israel of 45:17.

readings.first: 'In the LORD shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory': the descendants as a body.
readings.second: 'In the LORD shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory': the descendants as a body.

readings.words: O house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel
readings.first: 'O house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, which are borne by me from the belly': the nation addressed.
readings.second: 'Hearken unto me, O house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel': the nation addressed.

readings.first: 'O house of Jacob, which are called by the name of Israel, and are come forth out of the waters of Judah': the people bearing the name Israel. 'God of Israel' is God's title.
readings.second: 'O house of Jacob, which are called by the name of Israel ... make mention of the God of Israel': the nation; Judah (13) is its source, not the record.

readings.first: 'shew my people their transgression, and the house of Jacob their sins': the nation addressed; the name Israel is not written.
readings.second: 'shew my people their transgression, and the house of Jacob their sins': the nation, parallel to 'my people'.

readings.first: 'the great goodness toward the house of Israel, which he hath bestowed on them': the nation as recipient.
readings.second: 'the great goodness toward the house of Israel, which he hath bestowed on them': the nation, 'my people' in 63:8.

readings.first: 'the house of Judah shall walk with the house of Israel, and they shall come together out of the land of the north': the northern nation as a body.
readings.second: 'the house of Judah shall walk with the house of Israel, and they shall come together out of the land of the north': the people returning.

readings.first: 'the house of Judah shall walk with the house of Israel, and they shall come together out of the land of the north': the nation acting.
readings.second: 'the house of Judah shall walk with the house of Israel ... come together out of the land of the north': the nation returning.

readings.first: 'so have ye dealt treacherously with me, O house of Israel': the nation addressed.
readings.second: 'so have ye dealt treacherously with me, O house of Israel': the nation addressed as an unfaithful wife.

readings.first: 'the house of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt very treacherously against me': the nation as a body.
readings.second: 'the house of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt very treacherously against me': the nation, beside Judah.

readings.first: 'the house of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt very treacherously against me': the nation acting.
readings.second: 'the house of Israel and the house of Judah have dealt very treacherously against me': the nation.

readings.first: 'Declare this in the house of Jacob, and publish it in Judah': the people addressed; the name Israel is not written.
readings.second: 'Declare this in the house of Jacob, and publish it in Judah': the nation, called 'O foolish people' in 5:21.

readings.first: 'O ye children of Benjamin, gather yourselves to flee out of the midst of Jerusalem': the tribe addressed as a body.
readings.second: 'O ye children of Benjamin, gather yourselves to flee out of the midst of Jerusalem': the tribe addressed as a body by the prophet.

readings.first: 'as I have cast out all your brethren, even the whole seed of Ephraim': the tribe's descendants, cast out.
readings.second: 'as I have cast out all your brethren, even the whole seed of Ephraim': the Ephraimite people cast out by God.

readings.first: 'Egypt, and Judah, and Edom, and the children of Ammon, and Moab... all these nations are uncircumcised': the Ammonites as a nation.
readings.second: 'Egypt, and Judah, and Edom, and the children of Ammon, and Moab ... all these nations are uncircumcised': a nation.

readings.first: 'Hear ye the word which the LORD speaketh unto you, O house of Israel': the nation addressed.
readings.second: 'Hear ye the word which the LORD speaketh unto you, O house of Israel': the nation addressed.

readings.first: 'the house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken my covenant which I made with their fathers': the nation.
readings.second: 'the house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken my covenant which I made with their fathers': the nation.

readings.first: 'the house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken my covenant which I made with their fathers': the nation as a body.
readings.second: 'the house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken my covenant': the nation, the 'men of Judah' of 11:9.

readings.first: 'pluck out the house of Judah from among them': the nation uprooted from among its neighbours.
readings.second: 'pluck out the house of Judah from among them': the nation taken from among its neighbours.

readings.first: 'I caused to cleave unto me the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah... for a people': the nation.
readings.second: 'I caused to cleave unto me the whole house of Israel ... that they might be unto me for a people': the nation.

readings.first: 'I caused to cleave unto me the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah ... but they would not hear': the nation.
readings.second: 'caused to cleave unto me ... the whole house of Judah ... that they might be unto me for a people': the nation.

readings.first: 'O house of Israel, cannot I do with you as this potter... so are ye in mine hand, O house of Israel': the nation addressed.
readings.second: 'as the clay is in the potter's hand, so are ye in mine hand, O house of Israel': the nation addressed.

readings.first: 'I will give all Judah into the hand of the king of Babylon' names Jeremiah's own-time king of Babylon, Nebuchadrezzar (21:2, 25:1, 27:6).
readings.second: 'into the hand of the king of Babylon' is the king Jeremiah names in the same book, 21:2 'Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon maketh war against us' and 25:9.

readings.words: the seed of the house of Israel
readings.first: 'brought up and led the seed of the house of Israel out of the north country': the descendants gathered from the countries.
readings.second: 'led the seed of the house of Israel out of the north country ... they shall dwell in their own land': the people returned.

readings.first: 'Edom, and Moab, and the children of Ammon': the nation listed among those who drink the cup, beside other peoples.
readings.second: 'Edom, and Moab, and the children of Ammon': nations made to drink the cup, in a list of kings and peoples.

readings.first: 'in the house of the king of Judah' is the palace of the reigning king, whom 27:3 and 27:12 name as Zedekiah (Mattaniah, 2 Kings 24:17); the verse speaks of his house.
readings.second: 'the house of the king of Judah' is spoken after Jeconiah's deportation (27:20) to 'Zedekiah king of Judah' (27:12), the reigning king.
readings.settled: Kept, of the verse only: the message of the chapter goes to 'Zedekiah king of Judah' (27:3, 27:12), and 'the house of the king of Judah' is his; the word king is not given to him.

readings.first: 'in the house of the king of Judah' is the palace of the reigning king, whom 27:3 and 27:12 name as Zedekiah (Mattaniah, 2 Kings 24:17); the verse speaks of his house.
readings.second: 'the house of the king of Judah' is the house left after Jeconiah was carried away (27:20), in the message to 'Zedekiah king of Judah' (27:12).
readings.settled: Kept, of the verse only: as 27:18, the house of the reigning king, Zedekiah (27:12), after Jeconiah was carried away (27:20).

readings.first: 'I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man': the nation.
readings.second: 'I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man': the nation repopulated.

readings.first: 'I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man': the nation repopulated.
readings.second: 'I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of man': the nation repopulated.

readings.first: 'a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah': the nation as covenant partner.
readings.second: 'I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah': the nation whose fathers left Egypt (31:32).

readings.first: 'a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah': a covenant with the nation.
readings.second: 'a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah': the nation.

readings.first: 'the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel... they shall be my people': the nation.
readings.second: 'the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel ... they shall be my people': the nation.

readings.first: 'shut up in the court of the prison, which was in the king of Judah's house' in Zedekiah's tenth year (32:1), and 'Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up' (32:3).
readings.second: 'the court of the prison, which was in the king of Judah's house' is Zedekiah's, dated 'the tenth year of Zedekiah' (32:1); 'Zedekiah king of Judah had shut him up' (32:3).

readings.first: 'the children of Israel and the children of Judah have only done evil before me from their youth': the nation acting.
readings.second: 'the children of Israel and the children of Judah have only done evil before me from their youth': the nation.

readings.first: 'the evil of the children of Judah ... their kings ... and the men of Judah, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem': the nation and its men.
readings.second: 'the evil of the children of Israel and of the children of Judah ... their kings, their princes ... and the men of Judah': the nation and its members.

readings.first: 'that good thing which I have promised unto the house of Israel and to the house of Judah': the nation.
readings.second: 'that good thing which I have promised unto the house of Israel and to the house of Judah': the nation.

readings.first: 'the good thing which I have promised unto the house of Israel and to the house of Judah': the promise is to the nation.
readings.second: 'that good thing which I have promised unto the house of Israel and to the house of Judah': the nation.

readings.first: 'David shall never want a man to sit upon the throne of the house of Israel': the nation over which the throne rules.
readings.second: 'a man to sit upon the throne of the house of Israel': the throne of the nation, ruled by David's line.

readings.first: 'cast away the seed of Jacob... rulers over the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob': the descendants as a people; the name Israel is not written.
readings.second: 'cast away the seed of Jacob ... rulers over the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob': the descendants; Jacob (18) in the list of three patriarchs names the man.

readings.first: 'the house of Judah will hear all the evil ... that they may return every man from his evil way': the nation as hearers.
readings.second: 'the house of Judah will hear ... that they may return every man from his evil way': the nation.

readings.first: 'The king of Babylon shall certainly come and destroy this land' is Nebuchadrezzar, in Jehoiakim's fourth year (36:1), which Jer 25:1 calls his first year.
readings.second: The roll written in Jehoiakim's fourth year (36:1) warned that 'The king of Babylon shall certainly come'; that year is 'the first year of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon' (25:1).

readings.first: 'the king of Judah, that sent you unto me to enquire of me' is Zedekiah the king who sent Jehucal and Zephaniah (37:3), i.e. Mattaniah (2 Kings 24:17).
readings.second: 'the king of Judah, that sent you unto me to enquire' is 'Zedekiah the king' who sent Jehucal and Zephaniah to Jeremiah (37:3).

readings.first: 'thou shalt be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon' is said under Zedekiah, made king by 'Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon' (37:1), who besieged Jerusalem (39:1).
readings.second: Zedekiah is told 'thou shalt be delivered into the hand of the king of Babylon', the 'Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon' who made him king (37:1) and besieged him (39:1).

readings.first: 'The king of Babylon shall not come against you' is the false prophets' claim about Zedekiah's time's Babylonian king, Nebuchadrezzar (37:1, 39:1).
readings.second: 'The king of Babylon shall not come against you' in Zedekiah's reign means Nebuchadrezzar, who made him king (37:1) and came against Jerusalem (39:1).

readings.first: 'the hand of the king of Babylon's army' is that of Zedekiah's time's king of Babylon, Nebuchadrezzar, who made Zedekiah king (37:1) and besieged the city (39:1).
readings.second: 'the king of Babylon's army, which shall take it' is Nebuchadrezzar's army, which 39:1 says came against Jerusalem and besieged it.

readings.first: 'go forth unto the king of Babylon's princes' is said to Zedekiah; the king of Babylon then is Nebuchadrezzar (37:1, 39:1).
readings.second: Zedekiah is to 'go forth unto the king of Babylon's princes'; in his reign that king is 'Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon' (37:1, 39:1-3).

readings.first: 'if thou wilt not go forth to the king of Babylon's princes' is said to Zedekiah; that king of Babylon is Nebuchadrezzar (37:1, 39:1).
readings.second: 'the king of Babylon's princes' to whom Zedekiah must go forth are Nebuchadrezzar's, whose princes 39:3 lists at the gate.

readings.first: 'the women that are left in the king of Judah's house ... Thy friends have set thee on': the king is the 'thee' spoken to, Zedekiah (38:17-24), i.e. Mattaniah (2 Kings 24:17).
readings.second: Jeremiah speaks to Zedekiah (38:19, 38:24) of 'the women that are left in the king of Judah's house'; 'thee' and 'thy feet' also address him.

readings.first: 'brought forth to the king of Babylon's princes' is in the reign of Zedekiah; the king of Babylon then is Nebuchadrezzar (37:1, 39:1).
readings.second: The women 'brought forth to the king of Babylon's princes' in Zedekiah's reign go to Nebuchadrezzar's princes (37:1, 39:3).

readings.first: 'taken by the hand of the king of Babylon' is said to Zedekiah; that king is Nebuchadrezzar, who made Zedekiah king (37:1) and besieged Jerusalem (39:1).
readings.second: Zedekiah 'shalt be taken by the hand of the king of Babylon', the 'Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon' who made him king (37:1) and besieged Jerusalem (39:1).

readings.first: 'the captain of the guard gave him victuals and a reward, and let him go' and 'Go back ... unto thee' address the man taken in 40:2, 'took Jeremiah'; Jeremiah is marked only by suffixes.
readings.second: 'the captain of the guard gave him victuals and a reward, and let him go' is the Jeremiah he took in 40:2; 40:6 follows, 'Then went Jeremiah unto Gedaliah'.

readings.first: 'whom the king of Babylon hath made governor' follows the fall of Jerusalem, when 'Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon' gave orders (39:1, 39:11) and Nebuzaradan acted.
readings.second: Gedaliah is the one 'whom the king of Babylon hath made governor' after the fall; that king is 'Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon' who gave charge over Jeremiah to Nebuzaradan (39:11).

readings.first: 'the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah... governor' is the king of Babylon who took Jerusalem, Nebuchadrezzar (39:1, 39:11).
readings.second: 'the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah ... governor' after the fall of Jerusalem is Nebuchadrezzar, the conqueror of 39:1-11.

readings.first: 'serve the king of Babylon' is the king who made Gedaliah governor (40:7), Nebuchadrezzar of 39:1 and 39:11.
readings.second: 'serve the king of Babylon' in Gedaliah's oath after the fall refers to the reigning Nebuchadrezzar of 39:1-11 and 43:10.

readings.first: 'in Moab, and among the Ammonites, and in Edom': the Hebrew 'in the sons of Ammon' stands in a list of places where Jews were, so it could be the people or their land.
readings.second: 'the Jews that were in Moab, and among the Ammonites, and in Edom': Jews living among the people, named as a nation beside Moab and Edom.
readings.settled: Kept: 'among the Ammonites', the sons of Ammon, is where the Jews lived beside Moab and Edom: the people among whom they dwelt.

readings.first: 'the king of Babylon had left a remnant of Judah' is the conqueror of Jerusalem, Nebuchadrezzar (39:1, 39:11), who set Gedaliah over them.
readings.second: 'the king of Babylon had left a remnant of Judah, and that he had set over them Gedaliah' is Nebuchadrezzar, the conqueror of 39:1-11.

readings.first: Gedaliah, 'whom the king of Babylon had made governor over the land', was set by Nebuchadrezzar's commander after the fall of Jerusalem (39:11-14, 40:5).
readings.second: Gedaliah is the one 'whom the king of Babylon had made governor over the land', Nebuchadrezzar of 39:1-11 and 43:10.

readings.first: 'departed to go over to the Ammonites': Ishmael goes to the children of Ammon as a people to be received by, not merely to a place.
readings.second: 'departed to go over to the Ammonites': Ishmael goes over to the nation.

readings.first: 'Ishmael... escaped from Johanan with eight men, and went to the Ammonites': the people as refuge.
readings.second: 'escaped from Johanan with eight men, and went to the Ammonites': the nation he fled to.

readings.first: 'Gedaliah... whom the king of Babylon made governor' is the governor of 40:5, appointed by Nebuchadrezzar, king of Babylon (39:1, 39:11).
readings.second: Gedaliah, 'whom the king of Babylon made governor in the land', was appointed by Nebuchadrezzar after the fall (39:1-11); 43:10 still names him as king.

readings.first: 'Be not afraid of the king of Babylon' is said to the remnant under Gedaliah, whose king of Babylon is Nebuchadrezzar (39:1, 40:7).
readings.second: 'Be not afraid of the king of Babylon' is said to the remnant after Gedaliah's murder; the reigning king is 'Nebuchadrezzar the king of Babylon' of 43:10.

readings.first: The Hebrew prints 'Amon from Thebes' (words 9-11), which the King James renders 'the multitude of No', the very one punished in this verse.
readings.second: The Hebrew prints the name itself, 'Amon from No' (words 9-11), as the first object of 'I will punish'; the King James renders it 'the multitude of No'.

readings.first: 'as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel their confidence': the nation as a body.
readings.second: 'as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel their confidence': the nation, compared with Moab.

readings.first: 'Concerning the Ammonites, thus saith the LORD... their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities': the nation addressed, with king and people.
readings.second: 'Concerning the Ammonites ... why then doth their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities?': an oracle on the nation.

readings.first: 'an alarm of war to be heard in Rabbah of the Ammonites': the city is named as the Ammonite nation's city, whose daughters burn.
readings.second: 'an alarm of war to be heard in Rabbah of the Ammonites': the city is named as the people's, in an oracle against the nation (v.1).

readings.first: 'I will bring again the captivity of the children of Ammon': a captive nation restored.
readings.second: 'I will bring again the captivity of the children of Ammon': the nation's exiles restored.

readings.first: Nebuzaradan 'brought them to the king of Babylon to Riblah'; 52:28 names 'Nebuchadrezzar' as the one who carried the people away in this same account.
readings.second: Captives were brought 'to the king of Babylon to Riblah' in 'the nineteenth year of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon' (52:12); 52:28 names him as the one carrying them away.

readings.first: 'he did continually eat bread before him all the days of his life' follows 52:31-32, where Evilmerodach frees Jehoiachin; the eater is Jehoiachin, marked by the verb and 'his prison garments'.
readings.second: 'his prison garments' and 'he did continually eat bread' continue 52:31, where the king of Babylon brought 'Jehoiachin king of Judah' out of prison; Hebrew has only verb person and suffixes.

readings.first: 'a continual diet given him of the king of Babylon' is from Evilmerodach king of Babylon, who freed Jehoiachin in 52:31-33.
readings.second: 'a continual diet given him of the king of Babylon' continues the kindness of 'Evilmerodach king of Babylon' to Jehoiachin from 52:31-33.

readings.first: 'go, get thee unto the house of Israel, and speak with my words unto them': the nation as the prophet's hearers.
readings.second: 'get thee unto the house of Israel, and speak with my words unto them': the nation Ezekiel is sent to.

readings.first: 'not sent to a people of a strange speech... but to the house of Israel': the nation set against foreign peoples.
readings.second: 'not sent to a people of a strange speech ... but to the house of Israel': the nation, set against other peoples.

readings.first: 'the house of Israel will not hearken unto thee... all the house of Israel are impudent and hardhearted': the nation.
readings.second: 'the house of Israel will not hearken unto thee ... all the house of Israel are impudent and hardhearted': the nation.

readings.first: 'This shall be a sign to the house of Israel': the nation as audience of the sign.
readings.second: 'This shall be a sign to the house of Israel': the nation shown the siege of Jerusalem.

readings.first: 'lay the iniquity of the house of Israel upon it... thou shalt bear their iniquity': the nation's guilt.
readings.second: 'lay the iniquity of the house of Israel upon it ... thou shalt bear their iniquity': the nation's guilt.

readings.first: 'so shalt thou bear the iniquity of the house of Israel': the nation's guilt.
readings.second: 'so shalt thou bear the iniquity of the house of Israel': the nation's guilt, beside Judah's in 4:6.

readings.first: 'thou shalt bear the iniquity of the house of Judah forty days': the nation's guilt, set beside that of the house of Israel.
readings.second: 'thou shalt bear the iniquity of the house of Judah forty days': the nation's iniquity.

readings.first: 'a fire come forth into all the house of Israel': the whole nation affected.
readings.second: 'thereof shall a fire come forth into all the house of Israel': the whole nation.

readings.first: 'Alas for all the evil abominations of the house of Israel! for they shall fall by the sword': the nation.
readings.second: 'Alas for all the evil abominations of the house of Israel! for they shall fall by the sword': the nation.

readings.first: 'all the idols of the house of Israel, pourtrayed upon the wall': the nation whose idols these are.
readings.second: 'all the idols of the house of Israel, pourtrayed upon the wall': the nation's idols.

readings.first: 'seventy men of the ancients of the house of Israel': elders of the nation.
readings.second: 'seventy men of the ancients of the house of Israel': elders of the nation.

readings.first: 'what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark': elders of the nation.
readings.second: 'what the ancients of the house of Israel do in the dark': elders of the nation.

readings.first: 'Is it a light thing to the house of Judah that they commit the abominations': the nation addressed, 'they'.
readings.second: 'Is it a light thing to the house of Judah that they commit the abominations': the nation.

readings.first: 'The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceeding great': the nation's guilt.
readings.second: 'The iniquity of the house of Israel and Judah is exceeding great ... for they say': the nation; Judah (8) is named beside it, not counted here.

readings.words: all the house of Israel wholly
readings.first: 'thy brethren... and all the house of Israel wholly, are they unto whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem have said': the nation as a body.
readings.second: 'thy brethren ... and all the house of Israel wholly, are they unto whom the inhabitants of Jerusalem have said': the exiled nation.

readings.first: 'I have set thee for a sign unto the house of Israel': the nation as audience.
readings.second: 'I have set thee for a sign unto the house of Israel': the nation that watches the prophet.

readings.first: 'hath not the house of Israel, the rebellious house, said unto thee, What doest thou?': the nation speaking.
readings.second: 'hath not the house of Israel, the rebellious house, said unto thee': the nation.

readings.first: 'no more any vain vision nor flattering divination within the house of Israel': the nation as a community.
readings.second: 'no more any vain vision nor flattering divination within the house of Israel': the nation.

readings.words: they of the house of Israel
readings.first: 'they of the house of Israel say, The vision that he seeth is for many days to come': the nation speaking.
readings.second: 'they of the house of Israel say, The vision that he seeth is for many days to come': the nation speaking.

readings.first: 'neither made up the hedge for the house of Israel to stand in the battle in the day of the LORD': the nation in war.
readings.second: 'neither made up the hedge for the house of Israel to stand in the battle': the nation left unprotected by its prophets.

readings.first: 'Every man of the house of Israel that setteth up his idols in his heart': members of the nation.
readings.second: 'Every man of the house of Israel that setteth up his idols in his heart': members of the nation.

readings.first: 'Therefore say unto the house of Israel... Repent, and turn yourselves from your idols': the nation addressed.
readings.second: 'say unto the house of Israel ... Repent, and turn yourselves from your idols': the nation addressed.

readings.first: 'every one of the house of Israel, or of the stranger that sojourneth in Israel': members of the nation; the second 'Israel' may be land or people, so only the first is marked.
readings.second: 'every one of the house of Israel, or of the stranger that sojourneth in Israel': the nation; 'in Israel' (14) is where the stranger lives, people or land, so left out.

readings.first: 'the house of Israel may go no more astray from me... that they may be my people': the nation.
readings.second: 'That the house of Israel may go no more astray from me ... that they may be my people': the nation.

readings.first: 'speak a parable unto the house of Israel': the nation as audience.
readings.second: 'put forth a riddle, and speak a parable unto the house of Israel': the nation addressed.

readings.first: 'the king of Babylon is come to Jerusalem, and hath taken the king thereof' is the Nebuchadrezzar of 2KI 24:10-12 and Ezekiel's own-time king of Babylon (26:7, 29:18).
readings.second: 'the king of Babylon is come to Jerusalem, and hath taken the king thereof' is the king of Ezekiel's day, whom the book names 'Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon' (26:7, 29:18).

readings.first: 'lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel': the nation's idols.
readings.second: 'neither hath lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel': the idols the nation worships.

readings.first: 'lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel': the nation's idols.
readings.second: 'neither hath lifted up his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel': the idols the nation worships.

readings.first: 'Hear now, O house of Israel; Is not my way equal?': the nation addressed.
readings.second: 'Hear now, O house of Israel; Is not my way equal? are not your ways unequal?': the nation addressed.

readings.first: 'Yet saith the house of Israel, The way of the Lord is not equal. O house of Israel, are not my ways equal?': the nation speaking and addressed.
readings.second: 'Yet saith the house of Israel, The way of the Lord is not equal. O house of Israel': the nation speaking and addressed.

readings.first: 'I will judge you, O house of Israel, every one according to his ways': the nation addressed.
readings.second: 'I will judge you, O house of Israel, every one according to his ways': the nation addressed.

readings.first: 'for why will ye die, O house of Israel?': the nation addressed.
readings.second: 'for why will ye die, O house of Israel?': the nation addressed.

readings.first: 'brought him to the king of Babylon' is the king of Babylon of Ezekiel's time, Nebuchadrezzar (26:7, 29:18), to whom Judah's kings were carried.
readings.second: The captured lion of the lament is 'brought ... to the king of Babylon', the king who took Judah's king in Ezekiel's time, named 'Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon' in 26:7.

readings.first: 'the house of Israel rebelled against me in the wilderness: they walked not in my statutes': the nation.
readings.second: 'the house of Israel rebelled against me in the wilderness: they walked not in my statutes': the nation.

readings.first: 'speak unto the house of Israel... in this your fathers have blasphemed me': the nation addressed.
readings.second: 'speak unto the house of Israel ... in this your fathers have blasphemed me': the nation addressed.

readings.first: 'As for you, O house of Israel... Go ye, serve ye every one his idols': the nation addressed.
readings.second: 'As for you, O house of Israel ... serve ye every one his idols': the nation addressed.

readings.first: 'when I have wrought with you for my name's sake... O ye house of Israel': the nation addressed.
readings.second: 'not according to your wicked ways ... O ye house of Israel': the nation addressed.

readings.first: 'the sword of the king of Babylon may come' to Jerusalem is Nebuchadrezzar's attack, the king of Babylon of Ezekiel's time (26:7, 29:18, 30:10).
readings.second: 'the sword of the king of Babylon' coming against Jerusalem is that of the besieging king of Ezekiel's day, named 'Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon' in 26:7 and 29:18.

readings.first: 'the sword may come to Rabbath of the Ammonites, and to Judah in Jerusalem': the city named as the Ammonites' city, paired with Judah's.
readings.second: 'that the sword may come to Rabbath of the Ammonites': the city is named as the people's, set beside Judah in Jerusalem.

readings.first: 'the king of Babylon stood at the parting of the way' is the same king whose sword comes on Jerusalem (21:19-20), Nebuchadrezzar (26:7).
readings.second: 'the king of Babylon stood at the parting of the way' and chose Jerusalem; in Ezekiel's time that king is 'Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon' (26:7, 29:18).

readings.first: 'Thus saith the Lord GOD concerning the Ammonites, and concerning their reproach': the nation and its reproach.
readings.second: 'concerning the Ammonites, and concerning their reproach': a prophecy against the nation and its reproach.

readings.first: 'the house of Israel is to me become dross: all they are brass, and tin, and iron, and lead': the nation as a body.
readings.second: 'the house of Israel is to me become dross: all they are brass, and tin': the nation.

readings.first: 'the king of Babylon set himself against Jerusalem this same day', the tenth day of the tenth month of the ninth year, is the siege that Jer 52:4 ties to Nebuchadrezzar.
readings.second: 'the king of Babylon set himself against Jerusalem this same day' in the ninth year is the king of Ezekiel's day, named 'Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon' in 26:7 and 29:18.

readings.first: 'Speak unto the house of Israel, Thus saith the Lord GOD; I will profane my sanctuary': the nation addressed.
readings.second: 'Speak unto the house of Israel ... your sons and your daughters ... shall fall by the sword': the nation addressed.

readings.first: 'set thy face against the Ammonites, and prophesy against them': the nation addressed as a body, then 'them'.
readings.second: 'set thy face against the Ammonites, and prophesy against them': the nation addressed.

readings.first: 'say unto the Ammonites... Because thou saidst, Aha, against my sanctuary': the nation addressed and accused.
readings.second: 'say unto the Ammonites, Hear the word ... Because thou saidst, Aha': the nation addressed for its gloating.

readings.first: 'against the house of Judah, when they went into captivity': the nation, taken into exile.
readings.second: 'against the house of Judah, when they went into captivity': the nation exiled.

readings.first: 'I will make Rabbah a stable for camels, and the Ammonites a couching place for flocks': the people named beside their city.
readings.second: 'Rabbah a stable for camels, and the Ammonites a couching place for flocks: and ye shall know': the people addressed, though the image is their country laid waste.

readings.first: 'the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen': Moab and Seir speak of the nation.
readings.second: 'the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen': the nation compared with other nations.

readings.first: 'with the Ammonites... that the Ammonites may not be remembered among the nations': the nation given over and forgotten among nations.
readings.second: 'that the Ammonites may not be remembered among the nations': a nation among the nations.

readings.first: 'Edom hath dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance ... revenged himself upon them': the nation wronged.
readings.second: 'Edom hath dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance ... revenged himself upon them': the nation.

readings.first: 'no more a pricking brier unto the house of Israel, nor any grieving thorn of all that are round about them': the nation and its neighbours.
readings.second: 'no more a pricking brier unto the house of Israel, nor any grieving thorn of all that are round about them': the nation.

readings.first: 'a staff of reed to the house of Israel': the nation that Egypt leaned on, a body and not the man Jacob.
readings.second: 'they have been a staff of reed to the house of Israel': the nation that leaned on Egypt.

readings.first: 'no more the confidence of the house of Israel, which bringeth their iniquity to remembrance': a body that trusts and looks after Egypt.
readings.second: 'no more the confidence of the house of Israel': the nation that trusted Egypt.

readings.first: 'cause the horn of the house of Israel to bud forth': the nation's strength restored, with 'the midst of them'.
readings.second: 'cause the horn of the house of Israel to bud forth': the nation restored.

readings.first: 'I will strengthen the arms of the king of Babylon' against Pharaoh and Egypt is the Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon named for the same act in 30:10.
readings.second: The oracle against Egypt says in 30:10 'by the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon'; 'the arms of the king of Babylon' here are his.

readings.first: 'The sword of the king of Babylon shall come upon thee', said of Egypt, is Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon, who comes against Egypt in 30:10.
readings.second: 'The sword of the king of Babylon shall come upon thee', Egypt, echoes 30:10 'by the hand of Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon' and 29:19.

readings.first: 'I have set thee a watchman unto the house of Israel ... warn them': the prophet is sent to the nation as a body.
readings.second: 'I have set thee a watchman unto the house of Israel ... warn them': the nation Ezekiel warns.

readings.first: 'speak unto the house of Israel; Thus ye speak ... our transgressions': the nation addressed and speaking in the first person plural.
readings.second: 'speak unto the house of Israel ... our transgressions ... be upon us': the nation speaking of its sins.

readings.first: 'turn ye ... why will ye die, O house of Israel?': the nation addressed as 'ye'.
readings.second: 'why will ye die, O house of Israel?': the nation addressed in the plural.

readings.first: 'O ye house of Israel, I will judge you every one after his ways': the nation addressed and judged person by person.
readings.second: 'O ye house of Israel, I will judge you every one after his ways': the nation addressed.

readings.first: 'they, even the house of Israel, are my people': the nation itself is named as God's people.
readings.second: 'they, even the house of Israel, are my people': the nation as God's people.

readings.first: 'the inheritance of the house of Israel': the body that owns the inheritance and whose desolation Edom rejoiced at; the name stands for the nation, its lot.
readings.second: 'the inheritance of the house of Israel, because it was desolate': the nation's inheritance, over which Edom rejoiced.

readings.first: 'I will multiply men upon you, all the house of Israel, even all of it': the whole nation as inhabitants of the mountains.
readings.second: 'I will multiply men upon you, all the house of Israel, even all of it': the nation resettled on the mountains.

readings.first: 'when the house of Israel dwelt in their own land, they defiled it': the nation acting, not the land or the man.
readings.second: 'when the house of Israel dwelt in their own land, they defiled it': the nation's conduct.

readings.first: 'say unto the house of Israel ... I do not this for your sakes, O house of Israel': the nation addressed twice.
readings.second: 'say unto the house of Israel ... not this for your sakes, O house of Israel': the nation addressed twice.

readings.first: 'be ashamed and confounded for your own ways, O house of Israel': the nation addressed as 'ye'.
readings.second: 'be ashamed and confounded for your own ways, O house of Israel': the nation addressed.

readings.first: 'these bones are the whole house of Israel: behold, they say, Our bones are dried': the nation speaking as a body.
readings.second: 'these bones are the whole house of Israel: behold, they say': the nation in the vision of dry bones.

readings.first: 'seven months shall the house of Israel be burying of them': the nation acts, burying the dead to cleanse the land.
readings.second: 'seven months shall the house of Israel be burying of them': the nation burying Gog's host.

readings.first: 'the house of Israel shall know that I am the LORD their God': the nation as a knowing body.
readings.second: 'the house of Israel shall know that I am the LORD their God': the nation.

readings.first: 'the house of Israel went into captivity for their iniquity ... they trespassed against me': the nation carried off for its sin.
readings.second: 'the house of Israel went into captivity for their iniquity': the nation exiled.

readings.first: 'I have poured out my spirit upon the house of Israel': the nation receives the spirit, 'from them' before it.
readings.second: 'I have poured out my spirit upon the house of Israel': the nation gathered back.

readings.first: 'declare all that thou seest to the house of Israel': the nation as hearers of the prophet.
readings.second: 'declare all that thou seest to the house of Israel': the nation Ezekiel reports to.

readings.first: 'the sons of Zadok among the sons of Levi, which come near to the LORD to minister': the tribe as a body.
readings.second: 'these are the sons of Zadok among the sons of Levi, which come near to the LORD': the tribe out of which the Zadokites come.

readings.first: 'shew the house to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their iniquities': the nation with its sins.
readings.second: 'shew the house to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their iniquities': the nation.

readings.first: 'say to the rebellious, even to the house of Israel ... O ye house of Israel, let it suffice you of all your abominations': the nation addressed.
readings.second: 'to the rebellious, even to the house of Israel ... O ye house of Israel ... your abominations': the nation addressed twice.

readings.first: 'maidens of the seed of the house of Israel': the nation's descendants as a body from which priests may marry.
readings.second: 'maidens of the seed of the house of Israel': the priests' wives drawn from the nation's descendants.

readings.first: 'it shall be for the whole house of Israel': the city's possession belongs to the nation as a body.
readings.second: 'it shall be for the whole house of Israel': the city's possession belongs to the nation.

readings.first: 'all solemnities of the house of Israel ... reconciliation for the house of Israel': the nation keeping feasts and atoned for.
readings.second: 'all solemnities of the house of Israel ... to make reconciliation for the house of Israel': the nation's feasts and atonement.

readings.first: 'Thou, O king, art a king of kings' is Daniel speaking to the king whose dream he tells, 'the king Nebuchadnezzar' (2:28, 2:46).
readings.second: Daniel interprets the dream of 'the king Nebuchadnezzar' (2:28); 'Thou, O king, art a king of kings' addresses him.

readings.first: 'he came near where I stood... I was afraid' is spoken by the narrator, who is 'I, even I Daniel' in 8:15; only the verb ending and suffixes carry it.
readings.second: 'he said unto me, Understand, O son of man' addresses the speaker, who is 'I Daniel' in 8:15.

readings.first: 'Edom, and Moab, and the chief of the children of Ammon' escape the king's hand: the Ammonite nation, named with Edom and Moab.
readings.second: 'these shall escape out of his hand, even Edom, and Moab, and the chief of the children of Ammon': a nation beside Edom and Moab.

readings.first: 'I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away': the nation and 'them'.
readings.second: 'I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away': the northern nation.

readings.first: 'I will have mercy upon the house of Judah, and will save them by the LORD their God': the nation shown mercy.
readings.second: 'I will have mercy upon the house of Judah, and will save them': the nation, against the house of Israel.

readings.first: 'the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head': the nation gathered.
readings.second: 'the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head': the nation.

readings.first: 'hearken, ye house of Israel ... judgment is toward you': the nation addressed beside priests and the house of the king.
readings.second: 'hearken, ye house of Israel ... ye have been a snare on Mizpah': the nation addressed alongside priests and royal house.

readings.first: 'and sent to king Jareb' prints the king's own name.
readings.second: 'sent to king Jareb: yet could he not heal you' prints the name Jareb, the king named again in HOS 10:6; 'he' also refers to him.

readings.first: 'The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians': members of the nation sold.
readings.second: 'The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians': the people sold as captives.

readings.first: 'I will sell your sons and your daughters into the hand of the children of Judah': the nation as the buyer and seller.
readings.second: 'sell your sons and your daughters into the hand of the children of Judah': the people as buyers.

readings.first: 'the violence against the children of Judah, because they have shed innocent blood in their land': the nation wronged.
readings.second: 'for the violence against the children of Judah, because they have shed innocent blood in their land': the people wronged.

readings.first: 'For three transgressions of the children of Ammon... they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead': the nation's deeds.
readings.second: 'For three transgressions of the children of Ammon ... because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead': the nation's deeds.

readings.first: 'testify in the house of Jacob': the nation addressed under the ancestor's name; the same chapter calls it 'the children of Israel' (3:12) and 'Israel' (3:14).
readings.second: 'testify in the house of Jacob': the nation called by its ancestor's name, the 'children of Israel' of 3:12.

readings.first: 'Hear ye this word which I take up against you, even a lamentation, O house of Israel': the nation addressed.
readings.second: 'Hear ye this word ... a lamentation, O house of Israel': the nation addressed.

readings.first: 'The city that went out by a thousand shall leave an hundred ... to the house of Israel': the nation loses its fighting men.
readings.second: 'shall leave ten, to the house of Israel': the nation's cities decimated.

readings.first: 'thus saith the LORD unto the house of Israel, Seek ye me, and ye shall live': the nation addressed as 'ye'.
readings.second: 'thus saith the LORD unto the house of Israel, Seek ye me, and ye shall live': the nation addressed.

readings.first: 'the chief of the nations, to whom the house of Israel came': the nation as a body coming to its leaders.
readings.second: 'the chief of the nations, to whom the house of Israel came': the nation resorting to its leaders in Zion and Samaria.

readings.first: 'I will raise up against you a nation, O house of Israel': the nation addressed as 'you' and afflicted.
readings.second: 'I will raise up against you a nation, O house of Israel ... they shall afflict you': the nation addressed.

readings.first: 'I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob': the nation spared, set against 'the sinful kingdom'; the next verse calls it 'the house of Israel' (9:9).
readings.second: 'I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob': the nation of the sinful kingdom, called by its ancestor's name.

readings.first: 'I will sift the house of Israel among all nations, like as corn is sifted in a sieve': the nation scattered.
readings.second: 'I will sift the house of Israel among all nations': the nation scattered.

readings.first: 'neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction': the nation, addressed to Edom.
readings.second: 'neither shouldest thou have rejoiced over the children of Judah in the day of their destruction': the people.

readings.first: 'the house of Jacob shall possess their possessions': the nation in possession; the next verse sets it beside the houses of Joseph and Esau, and 1:20 names 'the children of Israel'.
readings.second: 'the house of Jacob shall possess their possessions': the nation, set against the house of Esau.

readings.first: 'the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame': the nation acting against the house of Esau.
readings.second: 'the house of Jacob shall be a fire ... the house of Esau for stubble': the nation devouring Edom.

readings.first: 'the transgression of Jacob ... the sins of the house of Israel. What is the transgression of Jacob? is it not Samaria?': Jacob stands for the nation, parallel to the house of Israel.
readings.second: 'the transgression of Jacob ... the sins of the house of Israel ... is it not Samaria?': the nation whose sin is its capital; Judah is named separately.

readings.first: 'O thou that art named the house of Jacob': the nation addressed and reproached.
readings.second: 'O thou that art named the house of Jacob': the nation addressed, 'my people' of 2:8.

readings.first: 'O heads of Jacob, and ye princes of the house of Israel': the nation's rulers addressed; Jacob and Israel both stand for the people.
readings.second: 'O heads of Jacob, and ye princes of the house of Israel': the nation's rulers.

readings.first: 'ye heads of the house of Jacob, and princes of the house of Israel, that abhor judgment': the nation's rulers addressed.
readings.second: 'ye heads of the house of Jacob, and princes of the house of Israel': the nation's rulers who pervert equity.

readings.first: 'the revilings of the children of Ammon, whereby they have reproached my people': the nation reviles.
readings.second: 'the revilings of the children of Ammon, whereby they have reproached my people': the nation reviling Israel.

readings.first: 'Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah... the residue of my people shall spoil them': the nation judged.
readings.second: 'the children of Ammon as Gomorrah ... the remnant of my people shall possess them': the nation judged.

readings.first: 'ye were a curse among the heathen, O house of Judah, and house of Israel': the nation addressed beside Judah.
readings.second: 'O house of Judah, and house of Israel; so will I save you': the nation addressed; Judah is named as a separate house.

readings.first: 'as ye were a curse among the heathen, O house of Judah, and house of Israel': the addressed body, exiled among nations.
readings.second: 'as ye were a curse among the heathen, O house of Judah, and house of Israel; so will I save you': the nation addressed as a body.

readings.first: 'to do well unto Jerusalem and to the house of Judah': the body of the people is the object of the LORD's good.
readings.second: 'to do well unto Jerusalem and to the house of Judah: fear ye not': the nation in the post-exilic days, addressed in the plural.

readings.words: The family of the house of Levi
readings.first: 'The family of the house of Levi apart, and their wives apart': a clan of the Levite house mourning as a body.
readings.second: 'The family of the house of Levi apart, and their wives apart': a mourning family of the land beside the house of David and of Nathan.

readings.first: 'he shall purify the sons of Levi... that they may offer unto the LORD an offering': the Levite body as offerers.
readings.second: 'he shall purify the sons of Levi, and purge them as gold and silver, that they may offer unto the LORD an offering': the priestly tribe.

readings.first: 'ye sons of Jacob are not consumed': the nation addressed as a body, not Jacob the man.
readings.second: 'therefore ye sons of Jacob are not consumed': the people addressed, whose 'fathers' went away from the ordinances (3:7).

readings.words: her that had been the wife of Urias
readings.first: 'of her that had been the wife of Urias' bore Solomon to David, and 2SA 11:3 and 12:24 tell that Bathsheba, wife of Uriah, bore Solomon.
readings.second: 'her that had been the wife of Urias', of whom David begat Solomon, retells 2SA 11:3 and 12:24, where Uriah's wife who bore Solomon is Bathsheba.

readings.first: 'took unto him his wife': Joseph was told 'fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife' (1:20), and Mary is the virgin of 1:23 who bore a son (1:25).
readings.second: 'took unto him his wife' obeys the angel's word 'fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife' (1:20).

readings.first: 'When he arose, he took the young child and his mother': the angel told Joseph 'Arise, and take the young child' (2:13), and 'he' does it.
readings.second: 'When he arose, he took the young child and his mother' obeys the angel's command to Joseph in 2:13; the article ho de stands for him.

readings.first: 'that it might be fulfilled ... Out of Egypt have I called my son': the verse itself applies the saying to the child taken to Egypt (2:13-14) and kept there 'until the death of Herod'.
readings.second: The verse itself applies 'Out of Egypt have I called my son' to the young child taken to Egypt in 2:14, whom 1:25 names Jesus; 'was there' is Joseph.

readings.first: 'And he arose, and took the young child and his mother': the angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph saying 'Arise, and take the young child' (2:19-20).
readings.second: 'And he arose, and took the young child and his mother' obeys the angel who appeared 'to Joseph in Egypt' (2:19-20); the article ho de stands for him.

readings.first: 'the tempter came to him' is 'the devil' who tempted Jesus in 4:1 and 4:5, and is addressed as 'Satan' in 4:10.
readings.second: 'the tempter' is 'the devil' of 4:1 by whom Jesus was to be tempted, whom Jesus names in 4:10 'Get thee hence, Satan'.

readings.first: 'when he was set, his disciples came unto him': the one who 'went up into a mountain' is Jesus of 4:23, followed by the crowds of 4:25 who were healed by him.
readings.second: 'when he was set, his disciples came unto him' continues 4:23, 'Jesus went about all Galilee', and 7:28 closes it, 'when Jesus had ended these sayings'.

readings.first: 'When he was come down from the mountain' follows 7:28 'when Jesus had ended these sayings' and continues with 8:3 'Jesus put forth his hand'.
readings.second: 'When he was come down from the mountain' follows 7:28, 'when Jesus had ended these sayings', and 8:3 names him, 'Jesus put forth his hand'.

readings.first: 'he entered into a ship, and passed over' continues 8:34 'the whole city came out to meet Jesus ... he would depart'; the subject is Jesus, marked only by the verb.
