readings.second: 'he entered into a ship, and passed over' follows 8:34, 'the whole city came out to meet Jesus ... besought him that he would depart'; Greek has only the verb's person.

readings.first: 'when he had called unto him his twelve disciples' follows 9:37 'saith he unto his disciples' and 9:35 'Jesus went about all the cities'; 10:5 names 'These twelve Jesus sent forth'.
readings.second: 'his twelve disciples' are those of the Jesus of 9:35, and 10:5 says 'These twelve Jesus sent forth'.

readings.first: 'go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel': the nation, in contrast to Gentiles and Samaritans (10:5).
readings.second: 'go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel': the nation, set against Gentiles and Samaritans.

readings.first: 'But he answered and said unto him that told him, Who is my mother?' replies to 12:47, where someone says 'thy mother and thy brethren', the speaker being Jesus of 12:46 'While he yet talked'.
readings.second: 'But he answered ... Who is my mother?' is the one teaching since 12:25 ('Jesus knew their thoughts'), whose mother stands without in 12:46; 13:1 names Jesus again.

readings.first: 'He answered and said unto them' replies to 13:10 'the disciples came, and said unto him, Why speakest thou unto them in parables?', after 13:1 'went Jesus out of the house'.
readings.second: 'He answered and said unto them' answers the disciples who 'said unto him, Why speakest thou unto them in parables?'; the speaker is the Jesus of 13:1.

readings.first: 'Another parable put he forth unto them' continues the parables of 13:1-23 that 13:34 attributes to Jesus: 'All these things spake Jesus unto the multitude in parables'.
readings.second: 'Another parable put he forth unto them' is the teller of the parables, Jesus of 13:1 and 13:34 ('All these things spake Jesus'); Greek has only the verb's person.

readings.first: 'when he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude' continues from 14:3-4, where Herod held John, and only the verb forms carry the subject.
readings.second: 'when he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude' continues 'Herod had laid hold on John' of 14:3; the Greek has only the verb forms, both 'him' being John.

readings.first: 'he called the multitude, and said unto them, Hear' is Jesus of 15:1, who next says 15:16 'Jesus said, Are ye also yet without understanding?'; only the verb marks him.
readings.second: 'he called the multitude, and said unto them' continues the answer of the Jesus to whom the scribes came in 15:1; 15:16 names him; Greek has only the verb's person.

readings.first: 'sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel': the nation, in contrast to the Canaanite woman.
readings.second: 'I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel': the nation, against the woman of Canaan.

readings.first: 'he sent away the multitude, and took ship' follows 15:34 'Jesus saith unto them, How many loaves have ye?' and the feeding of the four thousand; subject marked only by the verb.
readings.second: 'he sent away the multitude, and took ship' is the Jesus who fed them in 15:32-36; Greek has only the verb's person.

readings.first: The Pharisees and Sadducees 'desired him that he would shew them a sign'; 16:2 'He answered' and 16:6 'Jesus said unto them' show the one asked is Jesus.
readings.second: The Pharisees 'desired him that he would shew them a sign'; he is the one who came to Magdala in 15:39, named in 15:34 and 16:6 as Jesus.

readings.first: 'the Son of man is come to save' is Jesus' own title for himself (16:13 'that I the Son of man am'); the Greek of this verse is empty in Nestle 1904, so no word number exists.
readings.second: Jesus, speaking since 18:3, says 'the Son of man is come', his name for himself (16:13 'I the Son of man'); the verse is absent from the Greek shown, so no words.

readings.first: The children cry 'Hosanna to the son of David' at the wonders 'that he did'; 21:9 has the crowds cry the same to the one entering, and 21:16 'Jesus saith unto them' answers.
readings.second: The children cry 'Hosanna to the son of David' at the one doing wonders in the temple, Jesus of 21:12; 21:16 'Hearest thou what these say? And Jesus saith'.

readings.first: 'Master, we know that thou art true' is said by the Pharisees' disciples to the one they sought to 'entangle in his talk' (22:15); 22:18 has 'Jesus perceived their wickedness'.
readings.second: 'they sent out unto him their disciples ... saying, Master' addresses the one they would entangle in 22:15; 22:18 says 'But Jesus perceived their wickedness'.

readings.first: 'he had put the Sadducees to silence' refers to Jesus' answer of 22:29-32 ('Jesus answered ... I am the God of Abraham'); the subject is marked only by the verb.
readings.second: 'he had put the Sadducees to silence' is the answer of 22:29, 'Jesus answered and said unto them, Ye do err'; Greek has only the verb's person.

readings.first: 'one is your Master' is the one Jesus speaks of; 23:10 has 'one is your Master, even Christ', and Jesus is called Christ in 1:16; the KJV of 23:8 adds 'even Christ' too.
readings.second: 'one is your Master' has no 'Christ' in this Greek verse, but 23:10 says 'one is your Master, even Christ', and the book calls Jesus the Christ (16:16-20).

readings.first: 'many shall come in my name' is spoken by the one who 'answered and said unto them' in 24:4, 'Jesus answered'; the claimants who say 'I am Christ' are others.
readings.second: 'many shall come in my name' is said by the speaker of 24:4, 'And Jesus answered and said unto them'; the 'I' of 'I am Christ' is the deceivers'.

readings.first: The Greek has 'nor the Son, if not the Father' (οὐδὲ ὁ Υἱός), spoken by Jesus who says 'my words' (24:35) and speaks of 'the Son of man' (24:37); the KJV text omits 'neither the Son'.
readings.second: The Greek reads 'nor the Son', which the King James lacks (it has only 'my Father'); the speaker Jesus (24:4) calls himself the Son beside the Father in 11:27.

readings.first: Judas 'sought opportunity to betray him'; 26:15 'I will deliver him unto you' and 26:17 'the disciples came to Jesus' show the one betrayed is Jesus.
readings.second: Judas 'sought opportunity to betray him', the 'him' he offers to deliver in 26:15, who is the Jesus of 26:10 and 26:17.

readings.first: 'he sat down with the twelve' continues 26:19 'the disciples did as Jesus had appointed them'; 26:21 'he said, ... one of you shall betray me'; only the verb marks him.
readings.second: 'he sat down with the twelve' follows 26:19, 'the disciples did as Jesus had appointed them'; Greek has only the verb's person.

readings.first: 'Judas, which betrayed him, answered and said, Master, is it I? He said unto him, Thou hast said'; 26:26 names 'Jesus took bread' in the same meal.
readings.second: Judas 'which betrayed him' says 'Master, is it I?' to the one at table who foretold the betrayal, named in 26:26, 'Jesus took bread'.

readings.first: 'forthwith he came to Jesus, and said, Hail, master; and kissed him': the one who came with the crowd and gave the sign is Judas (26:47-48).
readings.second: 'he came to Jesus, and said, Hail, master; and kissed him' is Judas, who came in 26:47 and gave the sign of the kiss in 26:48; only the verbs carry him.

readings.first: 'whom they of the children of Israel did value': members of the nation priced him.
readings.second: 'whom they of the children of Israel did value': members of the nation who priced him.

readings.words: Thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days
readings.first: The passers-by revile the crucified one over whose head is 'THIS IS JESUS THE KING OF THE JEWS' (27:37): 'Thou that destroyest the temple ... If thou be the Son of God, come down from the cross'.
readings.second: The passers-by who 'reviled him' address the crucified one as 'Thou that destroyest the temple'; his title in 27:37 reads 'THIS IS JESUS'.

readings.first: Jesus speaks (28:18 'Jesus came and spake') and names 'the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost'; he calls God 'my Father' (26:39) and is called 'my beloved Son' (3:17).
readings.second: Jesus, speaking from 28:18, names 'the Son' beside 'the Father'; in this book he is that Son ('no man knoweth the Son, but the Father', 11:27; 'my beloved Son', 3:17).

readings.first: 'I send my messenger before thy face' with 'the voice of one crying in the wilderness' (1:3) is followed at once by 'John did baptize in the wilderness' (1:4).
readings.second: Mark joins the quotation 'Behold, I send my messenger before thy face' to 'John did baptize in the wilderness' (1:4) in one sentence, applying the messenger to John.

readings.first: 'he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed' follows 1:34 'he healed many' and 1:36 'followed after him'; the subject is marked only by the verbs.
readings.second: 'he went out, and departed into a solitary place' is the healer of 1:34, the Jesus of 1:25; 'Simon ... followed after him' in 1:36; Greek has only the verb's person.

readings.first: 'he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man' continues 2:25 'he said unto them' and follows 2:19 'Jesus said unto them'; the speaker is marked only by the verb.
readings.second: 'And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man' continues the answer of 2:25 by the Jesus of 2:19; Greek has only the verb's person.

readings.first: 'he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep' and they wake 'him' and say 'Master'; the same man rebukes the wind (4:39) and is 'Jesus' in 5:6.
readings.second: 'they awake him, and say unto him, Master' is the one they took 'as he was in the ship' (4:36); on landing the man 'saw Jesus' (5:6).

readings.first: 'his disciples follow him' follows 5:36 'Jesus heard the word' and leads to 6:4 'But Jesus, said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country'.
readings.second: 'his disciples follow him' into 'his own country' continues 5:36-43, and 6:4 names him: 'But Jesus, said unto them, A prophet is not without honour'.

readings.first: 'he constrained his disciples ... while he sent away the people' continues 6:34 'Jesus, when he came out' and the feeding of the five thousand; 6:46 'he departed into a mountain to pray'.
readings.second: 'he constrained his disciples ... while he sent away the people' is the Jesus of 6:34 who fed the five thousand.

readings.first: 'he arose, and went into the borders of Tyre ... he could not be hid' continues the same actor from 6:34 'Jesus' to 8:1 'Jesus called his disciples'; only the verbs mark him.
readings.second: 'from thence he arose, and went into the borders of Tyre' continues the teacher of 7:14-23, the Jesus of 6:34 and 8:1; Greek has only the verb's person.

readings.first: 'he took him aside ... and put his fingers into his ears': the man was brought to Jesus (7:32); the healer is the one of 7:31, who 'came unto the sea of Galilee'.
readings.second: In 'put his fingers into his ears' the first 'his' (word 12) is the healer's, to whom they bring the deaf man in 7:32, the Jesus of 6:34 and 8:1.

readings.first: 'And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you' continues 8:38, where the speaker says 'ashamed of me and of my words'; 9:2 names 'Jesus taketh with him Peter'.
readings.second: 'And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you' continues the speech of 8:34-38 by the Jesus of 8:27, and 9:2 names him; Greek has only the verb's person.

readings.first: A man of the crowd says 'Master, I have brought unto thee my son', to the one the people 'beheld' in 9:15, who 'answereth him' in 9:19 and is 'Jesus' in 9:23.
readings.second: 'Master, I have brought unto thee my son' answers the one who asked in 9:16; 9:23 names him, 'Jesus said unto him, If thou canst believe'.

readings.first: 'the Pharisees came to him, and asked him' follows 10:1 'he arose from thence ... he taught them again' and 10:5 'Jesus answered and said unto them'.
readings.second: 'the Pharisees came to him, and asked him' is the teacher of 10:1, and 10:5 names him: 'And Jesus answered and said unto them'.

readings.first: Bartimaeus cries 'Thou son of David' to the one he heard was 'Jesus of Nazareth', whom he earlier called 'Jesus, thou son of David' (10:47).
readings.second: 'Thou son of David, have mercy on me' repeats the cry of 10:47, 'Jesus, thou son of David', and 10:49 says 'Jesus stood still'.

readings.first: Peter says 'Master, behold, the fig tree which thou cursedst is withered away' to the one who cursed it, and the next verse has 'Jesus answering saith unto them'.
readings.second: Peter 'saith unto him, Master, behold, the fig tree which thou cursedst'; 11:22 answers, 'And Jesus answering saith unto them'.

readings.first: 'neither the Son, but the Father' is said by Jesus, who says 'my words' (13:31) and speaks of 'the Son of Man' (13:34); Mark 14:61-62 has him answer 'I am' to 'the Son of the Blessed'.
readings.second: The speaker Jesus (13:5) sets 'neither the Son' beside 'the Father'; this book calls him the Son ('This is my beloved Son', 9:7; 'the Son of the Blessed ... I am', 14:61-62).

readings.first: 'But he spake the more vehemently, If I should die with thee' follows 14:29 'Peter said unto him' and Jesus' words to him in 14:30; 'he' is Peter.
readings.second: 'But he spake the more vehemently, If I should die with thee' answers Jesus' word to Peter in 14:29-30, so 'he' is Peter.

readings.first: Judas 'goeth straightway to him, and saith, Master, master; and kissed him', the one he had betrayed (14:44), who 'answered' in 14:48: 'Jesus answered and said unto them'.
readings.second: Judas 'goeth straightway to him, and saith, Master, master; and kissed him'; the one seized is named in 14:48, 'And Jesus answered'.

readings.first: 'as soon as he was come, he goeth straightway to him, and saith, Master, master; and kissed him': the one who came with the crowd is Judas (14:43-44).
readings.second: 'he goeth straightway to him... and kissed him' is Judas of 14:43, who gave the kiss as a token (14:44); only the verbs carry him.

readings.first: 'But he held his peace, and answered nothing' follows 14:60 'the high priest ... asked Jesus', and 14:62 'Jesus said, I am'.
readings.second: 'But he held his peace ... the high priest asked him' is the Jesus questioned in 14:60, who answers in 14:62; 'the Christ' is only asked of him here.

readings.first: The superscription over the crucified one, after 15:24-25 'they crucified him', is the king of the Jews whom they saluted as 'King of the Jews' in 15:18 and whom Pilate questioned (15:2).
readings.second: 'THE KING OF THE JEWS' is written as 'his accusation' over the crucified one, whom Pilate calls 'him whom ye call the King of the Jews' (15:12), Jesus of 15:15.

readings.first: 'he bought fine linen, and took him down': the body was given to Joseph (15:45) and Joseph of Arimathaea had craved it (15:43); the verbs carry the subject.
readings.second: 'he bought fine linen, and took him down' follows Pilate giving 'the body to Joseph' (15:45); only the verbs carry Joseph, while 'him' is Jesus.

readings.first: 'he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever': a body ruled by a king, not the man; Jacob's house is the nation.
readings.second: 'he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever': the nation as his kingdom.

readings.words: that holy thing which shall be born of thee
readings.first: The angel tells Mary 'that holy thing which shall be born of thee', the son of 1:31 whose name she 'shalt call JESUS'.
readings.second: 'that holy thing which shall be born of thee' is the son promised to Mary in 1:31, 'bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS'.

readings.first: 'thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest' is said to the newborn whose name is John (1:13, 1:60, 1:63).
readings.second: Zacharias, filled with the Spirit (1:67), addresses his newborn son, named John in 1:63: 'And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest'.

readings.first: 'he shut up John in prison' is what 3:19 says of Herod the tetrarch, whom John reproved; the subject is only the verb ending.
readings.second: 'Added yet this above all, that he shut up John in prison' has 'Herod the tetrarch' of 3:19 as its subject; the Greek has only the verbs.

readings.first: The Greek prints 'Ἀδμεὶν' ('of Admin') as word 4 between Amminadab and Arni in the list; the King James text omits the name, but the original word names Admin.
readings.second: The Greek prints the name itself, word 4 'of Admin', between Amminadab and Arni; the King James follows another text and has only 'Aram' here, so no King James word stands for him.

readings.first: Luke 3:36 names Cainan, Arphaxad, Sem, Noe and Lamech; Shelah (Sala) stands at the end of 3:35, and Cainan is his father, not him.
readings.second: The chain continues from 3:35 'the son of Sala'; 'Which was the son of Cainan' makes Sala the son of Cainan, with no Greek word of its own for him.
readings.settled: Kept: 'Which was the son of Cainan' continues the chain from 'the son of Sala' that ends 3:35, as 3:38 continues from Cainan.

readings.first: 'Which was the son of Mathusala': the clause's subject is the Lamech who ends 3:36, the father of Noe, here given as son of Methuselah.
readings.second: 'Which was the son of Mathusala': the article tou continues the chain from 'the son of Lamech' ending 3:36, so it stands for Lamech, son of Methuselah.

readings.first: 'Which was the son of Enos': the first clause's subject is the Cainan who ends 3:37, given here as son of Enos; the verse itself names only Enos, Seth and Adam.
readings.second: 'Which was the son of Enos': the article tou continues the chain from 'the son of Cainan' ending 3:37, so it stands for Cainan, son of Enos.
readings.settled: Kept: 'Which was the son of Enos' continues the chain from 'the son of Cainan' that ends 3:37.

readings.first: Simon says 'Master, we have toiled all the night' to the one who taught from his ship (5:3-4); 5:8 has 'Simon Peter ... fell down at Jesus' knees'.
readings.second: Simon says 'Master ... at thy word I will let down the net' to the one teaching from his ship, named in 5:8: 'he fell down at Jesus' knees'.

readings.first: 'the company of his disciples' follows the twelve he chose (6:13-16) and the one who 'came down with them'; Jesus is the subject of 6:11 and 6:22.
readings.second: 'he came down with them' and 'his disciples' continue the one who chose the twelve in 6:13, named in 6:11 'what they might do to Jesus'.

readings.first: 'he went into a ship with his disciples' continues the speaker of 8:21 and leads to 8:28 'When he saw Jesus'.
readings.second: 'he went into a ship with his disciples' begins the crossing at whose end 8:28 names him: 'When he saw Jesus'.

readings.first: The disciples wake 'him' in the boat and cry 'Master, master'; the same one rebukes the wind and is named Jesus at 8:28.
readings.second: The disciples wake 'him' crying 'Master, master'; he is the one who entered the ship in 8:22 and is named on landing in 8:28, 'he saw Jesus'.

readings.first: The KJV sentence 'the Son of man is not come to destroy' is the speaker's own title (9:58 'Jesus said... the Son of man hath not'); the Greek shown here has no such words, only 'they went'.
readings.second: King James has Jesus say 'the Son of man is not come to destroy' (his self-title, 9:58), but Nestle prints only 'And they went to another village', so no original word carries it.

readings.first: 'as he was praying... one of his disciples said unto him, Lord, teach us' is the Lord Jesus of 10:41 and the teacher of 11:2.
readings.second: 'one of his disciples said unto him, Lord'; the one praying is the Jesus of 10:39-41, who then teaches them in 11:2.

readings.first: 'as he spake these things... said unto him' is the speaker of 11:2-26, who continues at 11:28-30 and speaks of 'the Son of man'.
readings.second: 'as he spake these things' is the speaker of 11:17-26, the one called 'Lord' in 11:1 and the 'Son of man' of 11:30; the woman says 'the womb that bare thee'.

readings.first: The lawyer answers the one who just said 'Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees' (11:44), addressing him 'Master'; that speaker is Jesus of 11:30.
readings.second: The lawyer 'said unto him, Master, thus saying thou reproachest us'; the one pronouncing the woes since 11:39 is 'the Lord', Jesus.

readings.first: One of the company says 'unto him, Master, speak to my brother'; he is the teacher of 12:1-12 who answers 'Man, who made me a judge' in 12:14.
readings.second: 'one of the company said unto him, Master'; he is the speaker of 12:1-12 who calls himself 'the Son of man' in 12:8-10.

readings.first: The blind man's cry 'Thou son of David, have mercy on me' repeats 18:38 'Jesus, thou son of David' to the passer-by Jesus of Nazareth (18:37).
readings.second: The blind man repeats his cry of 18:38, 'Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me'; 18:40 'And Jesus stood'.

readings.first: 'he sought to see Jesus... because he was little of stature' has only verb endings for its subject; he is the man named Zacchaeus, chief among the publicans, of 19:2.
readings.second: 'he sought to see Jesus ... because he was little of stature' continues from 'a man named Zacchaeus' in 19:2; the Greek has only the verbs' person.

readings.first: 'he answered and said unto them, I tell you' replies to 19:39 'Master, rebuke thy disciples'; only the verb 'He said' carries the person.
readings.second: 'he answered and said' is the one the Pharisees call 'Master' in 19:39, the Jesus set on the colt in 19:35; Greek has only the verb's person.

readings.first: 'he went into the temple, and began to cast out' continues Jesus of 19:41 and 19:46 'Saying unto them, It is written, My house'; only the verb carries the person.
readings.second: 'he went into the temple, and began to cast out' continues the Jesus of 19:35-41; Greek has no separate word, only the verb 'He began'.

readings.first: 'he answered and said unto them, I will also ask you one thing' answers 20:2 'by what authority doest thou these things' put to the teacher of 20:1; Jesus is named at 20:8.
readings.second: 'I will also ask you one thing; and answer me' is spoken by the one 20:8 names at the end of the same exchange: 'And Jesus said unto them'.

readings.first: 'And he beheld them, and said' is the speaker of the parable in 20:9-16 to the chief priests, named Jesus at 20:8.
readings.second: 'he beheld them, and said' is the teller of the parable begun in 20:9, the Jesus of 20:8; the Greek article in 'ho de' stands as the pronoun.

readings.first: The spies 'asked him, saying, Master, we know that thou sayest and teachest rightly'; he is the one of 20:19 'he had spoken this parable', named Jesus at 20:8.
readings.second: The spies 'asked him, saying, Master'; he is the one the chief priests watch in 20:19-20, named in 20:8 and 20:34.

readings.first: The Sadducees 'asked him' (20:27) and say 'Master, Moses wrote unto us'; he is the one answered by 'Jesus answering' at 20:34.
readings.second: The Sadducees who 'asked him' (20:27) say 'Master, Moses wrote unto us', and 20:34 has 'Jesus answering said unto them'.

readings.first: 'he said unto them, How say they that Christ is David's son?' is the one the scribes called 'Master' (20:39) and who is 'Jesus' at 20:34; the question about 'Christ' itself is not said to be himself.
readings.second: 'he said unto them' is the Jesus of 20:34 whom they 'durst not ask' in 20:40; 'Christ' here is the figure discussed, not said of himself in this verse.

readings.first: 'they asked him, saying, Master, but when shall these things be?' follows his words about the temple in 21:6; he is the speaker who says 'Son of man' at 21:27.
readings.second: 'they asked him, saying, Master'; he is the one teaching in the temple (21:5 'he said'), the Jesus of 20:34, who answers 'in my name' in 21:8.

readings.first: 'he sent Peter and John' is the one who says 'The Master saith unto thee... with my disciples' (22:11) and is addressed 'Where wilt thou' (22:9); Jesus is named at 22:47.
readings.second: 'he sent Peter and John' is the one Judas seeks to betray in 22:4-6, named in 22:47-48; Greek has only the verb 'He sent'.

readings.first: 'The Master saith... where I shall eat the passover with my disciples' is the sender's own title for himself, the one of 22:8 who sends Peter and John, named Jesus at 22:47.
readings.second: The sender of 22:8-10 tells them to say 'The Master saith unto thee ... with my disciples', speaking of himself; he is named Jesus in 22:47-48.

readings.first: He speaks of 'him that betrayeth me' (22:21) and 22:48 says 'Jesus said unto him, Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?'.
readings.second: After 'him that betrayeth me' (22:21) he says 'the Son of man goeth ... by whom he is betrayed'; 22:48 'Jesus said ... betrayest thou the Son of man'.

readings.first: 'Art thou the Christ? tell us' is put to the one they 'led... into their council' (22:66), held and mocked as Jesus in 22:63.
readings.second: 'Art thou the Christ?' is asked of the prisoner led into the council, whom 22:63 names: 'the men that held Jesus'.

readings.first: 'they began to accuse him... We found this fellow' concerns the one 'led... unto Pilate' (23:1), who is Jesus of 22:70.
readings.second: 'they began to accuse him, saying, We found this fellow' is the prisoner led to Pilate in 23:1, named in 23:8 'when Herod saw Jesus'.

readings.first: 'Pilate asked him, saying, Art thou the King of the Jews?' is the prisoner led to Pilate in 23:1, accused in 23:2, called Jesus in 23:8.
readings.second: 'Pilate asked him, saying, Art thou the King of the Jews?' is asked of the accused of 23:1-2, the Jesus Pilate sends to Herod in 23:7-8.

readings.first: The rulers deride the one crucified in 23:33, for whom Jesus prays in 23:34: 'let him save himself, if he be Christ, the chosen of God'.
readings.second: The rulers deride the crucified one, 'let him save himself, if he be Christ'; 23:34 names him, 'Then said Jesus, Father, forgive them'.

readings.first: One of the hanged malefactors 'railed on him' who bears 'THIS IS THE KING OF THE JEWS' (23:38); the other addresses him as 'Jesus' at 23:42.
readings.second: The malefactor 'railed on him, saying, If thou be Christ, save thyself'; the other then speaks 'unto Jesus' in 23:42.

readings.first: 'Why seek ye the living among the dead?' is said of the one whose body they did not find, 'the Lord Jesus' (24:3); 'He is not here, but is risen' (24:6).
readings.second: The women seek 'the body of the Lord Jesus' (24:3) and are asked 'Why seek ye the living among the dead?', explained by 24:6 'He is not here, but is risen'.

readings.first: 'the Word was made flesh' (1:14) is the one 'grace and truth came by' as 'Jesus Christ' (1:17), of whom John bears witness (1:15, 1:29-30).
readings.second: 'the Word' is the one 1:14 says 'was made flesh', of whom John bare witness (1:15), and John points him out as Jesus in 1:29-30; 1:17 'Jesus Christ'.

readings.first: 'In him was life' refers back to 'him' of 1:3, the Word of 1:1, who 'was made flesh' (1:14) and is Jesus Christ (1:17).
readings.second: 'In him was life' continues the 'him' of 1:3, the Word of 1:1, whom 1:14-17 and John's witness in 1:29-30 identify as Jesus Christ.

readings.first: 'the life was the light of men' belongs to 'him' of 1:4, the Word, who 'was made flesh' and came by Jesus Christ (1:14,17); the step from light to person is one of reading.
readings.second: 'the light shineth in darkness' is the Light John witnesses of (1:7-8), of whom 1:9-10 says 'the world was made by him'; but 1:4 makes it 'the life', so the step is loose.
readings.settled: Kept: the prologue makes the light a person: 'He was in the world, and the world was made by him' (1:9-10), the Word made flesh (1:14) that came by Jesus Christ (1:17).

readings.first: John 'came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light'; 1:15 says John 'bare witness of him' and 1:29-30 points to Jesus, so the Light is the one he witnessed.
readings.second: John came 'to bear witness of the Light'; 1:9-10 says of that Light 'the world was made by him', and John's witness in 1:29-34 is of Jesus.

readings.first: 'He was not that Light, but was sent to bear witness of that Light' names the Light John witnessed to, who is the Word and Jesus Christ (1:14,15,17).
readings.second: John 'was sent to bear witness of that Light'; the one he bears witness of is Jesus (1:15, 1:29-34), and 1:9-10 calls the Light 'him'.

readings.first: 'That was the true Light' is the one who 'was in the world, and the world was made by him' (1:10), the Word made flesh (1:14) and Jesus Christ (1:17).
readings.second: 'That was the true Light' runs on into 1:10 'He was in the world, and the world was made by him', the Word made flesh of 1:14-17, Jesus Christ.

readings.first: 'the Word was made flesh... the only begotten of the Father... full of grace and truth' is the one by whom 'grace and truth came', 'Jesus Christ' (1:17).
readings.second: 'the Word was made flesh ... full of grace and truth'; 1:15 'John bare witness of him' and 1:17 'grace and truth came by Jesus Christ' name him.

readings.first: Nathanael answers Jesus (1:47-48, 1:50): 'Rabbi, thou art the Son of God; thou art the King of Israel', calling him by titles.
readings.second: Nathanael 'saith unto him, Rabbi, thou art the Son of God', answering the Jesus of 1:47-48, and 1:50 has 'Jesus answered'.

readings.first: 'light is come into the world' follows God sending 'his Son into the world' (3:17); Jesus says 'I am the light of the world' (9:5) and 'I am come a light into the world' (12:46).
readings.second: 'light is come into the world' follows 3:17 'God sent ... his Son into the world', and in 12:46 Jesus says 'I am come a light into the world' (8:12).

readings.first: 'I am sent before him' is John's answer to 3:26 about the one 'that was with thee beyond Jordan', to whom John bore witness (1:29-34) as Jesus; 3:30 'He must increase'.
readings.second: John's 'I am sent before him' answers 3:26 about 'he ... to whom thou barest witness', the Jesus of 3:22, as in 1:30 'This is he of whom I said'.

readings.words: a man, which told me all things that ever I did
readings.first: The woman of 4:7-28 speaks of the man who talked with her at the well, Jesus (4:26), and asks 'is not this the Christ?'.
readings.second: 'a man, which told me all things that ever I did' is the Jesus who spoke with her at the well (4:16-19, 4:26); 4:30 'they ... came unto him'.

readings.first: 'his disciples prayed him, saying, Master, eat' addresses the Jesus of 4:26 and 4:34, who answers them 'I have meat to eat' (4:32).
readings.second: 'his disciples prayed him, saying, Master, eat'; 4:34 'Jesus saith unto them, My meat is to do the will of him that sent me'.

readings.first: The crowd 'found him on the other side of the sea' after 'seeking for Jesus' (6:24) and he answers 'Jesus answered them' (6:26); they call him 'Rabbi'.
readings.second: The people 'seeking for Jesus' (6:24) 'found him' and 'said unto him, Rabbi'; 6:26 'Jesus answered them'.

readings.first: 'he speaketh boldly, and they say nothing unto him' is the one they seek to kill (7:25), who is the Jesus teaching in the temple in 7:14 and 7:28.
readings.second: 'he speaketh boldly, and they say nothing unto him' is said of the one teaching in the temple, 7:14 and 7:28 'Then cried Jesus in the temple as he taught'.

readings.first: 'we know this man whence he is' answers the bold speaker of 7:26, whom Jesus replies to in 7:28 'Ye both know me, and ye know whence I am'.
readings.second: 'we know this man whence he is' is answered at once by 7:28 'Then cried Jesus ... ye know whence I am'; 'Christ' here is set against him.

readings.first: 'many of the people believed on him' and 'these which this man hath done' concern the one of 7:30 'his hour', who is Jesus of 7:28 and 7:33.
readings.second: 'many of the people believed on him' and ask of miracles 'which this man hath done'; he is the Jesus of 7:28 and 7:33.

readings.first: 'This is the Christ' is said by the crowd about the one whose saying they heard (7:40) and because of whom there was a division (7:43); Jesus cried in 7:37.
readings.second: 'Others said, This is the Christ' of the one whose saying they heard, 7:37 'Jesus stood and cried'; 7:43 'a division ... because of him'.

readings.first: 'his disciples asked him, saying, Master' follows 'as Jesus passed by, he saw a man which was blind' (9:1), and Jesus answers in 9:3.
readings.second: 'his disciples asked him, saying, Master' follows 9:1 'as Jesus passed by', and 9:3 has 'Jesus answered'.

readings.first: Jesus is the speaker ('Jesus answered', 9:3) and says of himself 'I am the light of the world'.
readings.second: 'As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world' continues the speech begun at 9:3 'Jesus answered'; Greek has only the verbs' first person.

readings.first: 'if any man did confess that he was Christ' refers to the one who opened the blind man's eyes (9:21), Jesus who made the clay (9:11, 9:14).
readings.second: 'if any man did confess that he was Christ' concerns the healer under inquiry, 9:14 'Jesus made the clay' and 9:16 'This man is not of God'.

readings.first: 'the Jews round about him... If thou be the Christ, tell us plainly' surround the one who 'walked in the temple' in 10:23, 'Jesus answered them' in 10:25.
readings.second: 'Then came the Jews round about him' follows 10:23 'Jesus walked in the temple', and 10:25 has 'Jesus answered them'.

readings.first: Jesus speaks ('Jesus answered them', 10:34) of 'him, whom the Father hath sanctified, and sent into the world' and says 'because I said, I am the Son of God'.
readings.second: Jesus (10:34 'Jesus answered them') speaks of himself as 'him, whom the Father hath sanctified, and sent into the world ... because I said, I am the Son of God'.

readings.first: 'His disciples say unto him, Master, the Jews of late sought to stone thee' addresses the one who 'saith he to his disciples' (11:7) and 'Jesus answered' (11:9).
readings.second: 'His disciples say unto him, Master, the Jews of late sought to stone thee'; he is the Jesus of 11:5-7, and 11:9 has 'Jesus answered'.

readings.first: 'he bearing his cross went forth' follows 'they took Jesus, and led him away' (19:16) and precedes 'Jesus in the midst' (19:18).
readings.second: 'he bearing his cross went forth' follows 19:16 'they took Jesus, and led him away', and 19:18 has 'Jesus in the midst'.

readings.first: 'another king, which knew not Joseph' is the king 'in which time Moses was born' (7:20), retelling Exodus 1, whose king is called Pharaoh in Exo 1:19.
readings.second: Stephen's 'another king arose, which knew not Joseph' retells EXO 1:8; 7:19-20 says 'The same dealt subtilly ... In which time Moses was born'.

readings.first: 'to visit his brethren the children of Israel': Moses' own kin in Egypt, the nation.
readings.second: 'to visit his brethren the children of Israel': the nation in Egypt, Moses' kin.

readings.first: 'Moses, which said unto the children of Israel, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up': the nation addressed.
readings.second: 'Moses, which said unto the children of Israel, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up': the nation addressed.

readings.first: 'the Just One' whose coming was foretold and whom 'ye have been now the betrayers and murderers' is Jesus: Acts 3:13-15 says 'ye denied the Holy One and the Just... killed the Prince of life'.
readings.second: 'the Just One; of whom ye have been now the betrayers and murderers' matches 3:13-15, 'Jesus; whom ye delivered up ... ye denied the Holy One and the Just'.

readings.first: 'Saul the son of Cis, a man of the tribe of Benjamin': names the tribe, as the body Saul belonged to.
readings.second: 'Saul the son of Cis, a man of the tribe of Benjamin': the tribe to which Saul belonged.

readings.first: The Greek 'Having departed then they' (genitive 'autōn') is Paul and Barnabas (13:43), Barnabas being Joses the Levite of Cyprus (4:36); the KJV prints a different wording here.
readings.second: Nestle reads 'as they went out' (autōn), Paul and Barnabas after Paul's sermon, followed in 13:43; the King James instead reads 'the Jews were gone out', so no KJV words stand for Barnabas.
readings.settled: Kept, of the verse only: in Nestle 'as they went out' are Paul and Barnabas, whom 13:43 names; the King James reads 'the Jews' here.

readings.first: In the Greek, 'Having departed then they (αὐτῶν)' are Paul and Barnabas (13:43), shared with Barnabas; the KJV prints 'the Jews... gone out', another reading, so no KJV word stands for him.
readings.second: Nestle reads 'as they went out' (auton), Paul and his company preaching in the synagogue (13:16, 13:43 'Paul and Barnabas'); the King James reads 'the Jews were gone out', with no word for Paul.
readings.settled: Kept, of the verse only: in Nestle 'as they went out' are Paul and Barnabas, whom 13:43 names; the King James reads 'the Jews' here.

readings.first: 'Then came he to Derbe and Lystra' continues 'Paul chose Silas, and departed' and 'he went through Syria and Cilicia' (15:40-41), and 16:3 says 'Him would Paul have to go forth'.
readings.second: 'Then came he to Derbe and Lystra' continues 15:40-41 'Paul chose Silas ... And he went through Syria'; 16:3 names Paul again; the Greek has only the verb.

readings.first: 'appealed to Augustus' (the Emperor) is Paul's appeal 'unto Caesar' of 25:11-12, and 25:8 says he has offended nothing against Caesar.
readings.second: 'he himself hath appealed to Augustus' is the appeal of 25:11, 'I appeal unto Caesar', and 25:21 sets 'Augustus' and 'Caesar' side by side.

readings.first: 'the gospel of his Son' is the gospel 'concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord' (Romans 1:3); 1:7-8 also name Jesus Christ.
readings.second: 'the gospel of his Son' takes up 1:3, the gospel of God 'concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord'.

readings.first: 'Esaias crieth concerning Israel, Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved': the nation, counted.
readings.second: 'crieth concerning Israel, Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand': the nation counted.

readings.first: 'I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin': Paul names the tribe he belongs to.
readings.second: 'I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin': Paul names the tribe he belongs to.

readings.first: 'the last Adam' is set against the first man in 15:21-22 ('by man... in Christ shall all be made alive') and 15:47 'the second man is the Lord from heaven', i.e. Christ.
readings.second: 'the last Adam was made a quickening spirit' is the counterpart of Adam named in 15:22, 'as in Adam all die, even so in Christ shall all be made alive'; 15:47.

readings.first: 'the children of Israel could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses': the nation at Sinai.
readings.second: 'the children of Israel could not stedfastly behold the face of Moses': the nation at Sinai.

readings.first: 'Moses put a veil over his face, that the children of Israel could not stedfastly look': the nation.
readings.second: 'that the children of Israel could not stedfastly look to the end': the nation before Moses' veil.

readings.first: 'of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin, an Hebrew of the Hebrews': Paul's tribe, named.
readings.second: 'of the stock of Israel, of the tribe of Benjamin': Paul's tribal membership.

readings.first: 'ye also have a Master in heaven' follows 3:24 'ye serve the Lord Christ', so the heavenly Master is that Lord Christ.
readings.second: 'ye also have a Master in heaven' uses the same word as 3:24, 'ye serve the Lord Christ', the master the servants were just pointed to.

readings.first: 'thou, O man of God' is the addressee of the letter, named 'son Timothy' in 1:18 and 'O Timothy' in 6:20, and 6:11 is a direct address to him.
readings.second: 'But thou, O man of God' addresses the letter's recipient, 'Timothy, my own son' (1:2), called 'son Timothy' (1:18) and 'O Timothy' (6:20).

readings.first: 'as their's also was' (ἡ ἐκείνων, 'that of those [two]') looks back to 3:8 'Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses'; the pair includes Jambres.
readings.second: 'as their's also was' (ekeinon, 'of those') points back to the two of 3:8, 'Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses'.

readings.first: 'as their's also was' (ἡ ἐκείνων, 'that of those [two]') looks back to 3:8 'Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses'; the pair includes Jannes.
readings.second: 'as their's also was' (ekeinon, 'of those') points back to the two of 3:8, 'Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses'.

readings.words: an high priest after the order of Melchisedec
readings.first: 'Called of God an high priest after the order of Melchisedec' continues the Son of 5:8-9; 6:20 says 'Jesus, made an high priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec'.
readings.second: 'Called of God an high priest after the order of Melchisedec' is said of the 'he' of 5:8-9, the Christ of 5:5; 6:20 'Jesus, made an high priest ... after the order of Melchisedec'.

readings.first: 'To whom also Abraham gave a tenth part of all; ... King of Salem' is the Melchisedec, king of Salem, of 7:1.
readings.second: 'To whom also Abraham gave a tenth... King of righteousness... King of Salem' continues 'this Melchisedec, king of Salem' of 7:1; 'whom' also refers to him.

readings.words: they that are of the sons of Levi
readings.first: 'they that are of the sons of Levi, who receive the office of the priesthood, have a commandment to take tithes': the tribe of Levi as a body.
readings.second: 'they that are of the sons of Levi, who receive the office of the priesthood, have a commandment to take tithes of the people'.

readings.first: 'a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah': a covenant with the nations as bodies.
readings.second: 'a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah': the nation; Judah named apart.

readings.first: 'the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel ... they shall be to me a people': the nation.
readings.second: 'the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel ... they shall be to me a people': the nation.

readings.first: 'the chief Shepherd shall appear' is the Christ of 5:1, the 'Shepherd and Bishop of your souls' after Christ's suffering (2:21-25), whose appearing is that of Jesus Christ (1:7, 1:13).
readings.second: 'when the chief Shepherd shall appear' is the appearing the letter awaits, 1:7 'the appearing of Jesus Christ'; 2:25 'the Shepherd and Bishop of your souls' follows Christ in 2:21-24.

readings.first: 'the Word of life' whom they heard, saw and handled is 'the life... with the Father... manifested unto us' (1:2), declared as 'his Son Jesus Christ' (1:3).
readings.second: 'That which ... our hands have handled, of the Word of life' is neuter and explained in 1:2 as 'the life was manifested'; the letter never says the Word is Jesus, though 1:3 names him.
readings.settled: Kept, of the verse only: the Word of life handled and seen is 'that eternal life, which was with the Father, and was manifested unto us' (1:2), and 1:3 says the fellowship is 'with his Son Jesus Christ'.

readings.first: 'antichrist shall come' names the coming one whom the readers 'have heard' of; the same verse says many antichrists have arisen, so the coming one is set apart.
readings.second: 'ye have heard that antichrist shall come' prints the record's own name, the one who is coming.

readings.first: 'He is antichrist, that denieth the Father and the Son' names the antichrist as the one who denies that Jesus is the Christ.
readings.second: 'He is antichrist, that denieth the Father and the Son' prints the name with the article, though it is said of whoever denies that Jesus is the Christ.

readings.first: 'that spirit of antichrist, whereof ye have heard that it should come' names the antichrist and speaks of what is coming, matching 1JN 2:18; the person himself is not described.
readings.second: 'that spirit of antichrist, whereof ye have heard that it should come' prints the name and points back to the coming one of 2:18.

readings.first: 'This is a deceiver and an antichrist' applies the name to whoever confesses not Jesus Christ come in flesh, the same denial as 1JN 2:22; it is a class term as well.
readings.second: 'This is a deceiver and an antichrist' prints the name with the article in Greek, said of those who confess not 'Jesus Christ is come in the flesh'.

readings.words: one like unto the Son of man
readings.first: 'one like unto the Son of man' in the midst of the candlesticks says 'I am he that liveth, and was dead' (1:18), the 'Jesus Christ... first begotten of the dead' of 1:5.
readings.second: The 'one like unto the Son of man' says in 1:18 he 'was dead' and is alive, as 1:5 'Jesus Christ ... the first begotten of the dead'; 22:16 'I Jesus have sent ... in the churches'.

readings.first: 'when I saw him, I fell at his feet' is the one who says 'I am the first and the last' and 'was dead' (1:17-18), Jesus Christ the first begotten of the dead (1:5).
readings.second: 'when I saw him' is the figure of 1:13-16 who says 'I am the first and the last' and in 1:18 'was dead', as 1:5 'Jesus Christ ... the first begotten of the dead'.

readings.words: he that liveth, and was dead
readings.first: 'I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore' is Jesus Christ 'the first begotten of the dead' (1:5).
readings.second: The speaker of 1:17 goes on 'I am he that liveth, and was dead; and ... I am alive', matching 1:5 'Jesus Christ ... the first begotten of the dead'; Greek has only first-person verbs.

readings.words: the first and the last, which was dead, and is alive
readings.first: 'the first and the last, which was dead, and is alive' repeats 1:17-18 'I am the first and the last... was dead', said by Jesus Christ of 1:5.
readings.second: 'the first and the last, which was dead, and is alive' repeats the speaker's words in 1:17-18, and 1:5 calls Jesus Christ 'the first begotten of the dead'.

readings.first: 'Balaam, who taught Balac to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel': the nation was led to eat idol-meat and fornicate.
readings.second: 'to cast a stumblingblock before the children of Israel': the nation Balaam's counsel ensnared.

readings.first: 'the Son of God, who hath his eyes like unto a flame of fire, and his feet... like fine brass' matches the one of 1:14-15 who 'was dead' (1:18), Jesus Christ.
readings.second: 'the Son of God, who hath his eyes like unto a flame of fire' is the figure of 1:14-15; 1:5-6 'Jesus Christ ... unto God and his Father', 2:27 'my Father'.

readings.words: the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God
readings.first: 'the faithful and true witness' echoes 1:5 'Jesus Christ, who is the faithful witness'; he is the Amen and beginning of God's creation, the speaker of the letters.
readings.second: 'the Amen, the faithful and true witness' takes up 1:5, 'Jesus Christ, who is the faithful witness'; he speaks of 'my God' in 3:12.

readings.words: the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David
readings.first: 'the Root of David' is said in 22:16 by 'I Jesus... I am the root and the offspring of David'; here he has prevailed to open the book.
readings.second: 'the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David' is named by 22:16, 'I Jesus ... I am the root and the offspring of David'.

readings.words: a Lamb as it had been slain
readings.first: The Lamb is the one who prevailed (5:5-7) and is told 'thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us... by thy blood' (5:9), matching Jesus Christ who washed us in his blood (1:5) and the Root of David (22:16).
readings.second: 'a Lamb as it had been slain' takes the book the Root of David was to open (5:5, 22:16 'I Jesus'); 5:9 'redeemed us ... by thy blood' matches 1:5.

readings.first: 'fell down before the Lamb' is the Lamb of 5:6 who took the book (5:7) and was slain and redeemed us by his blood (5:9), i.e. Jesus Christ of 1:5.
readings.second: They 'fell down before the Lamb' and sing 'thou wast slain, and hast redeemed us to God by thy blood' (5:9), as 1:5 'Jesus Christ ... washed us ... in his own blood'.

readings.first: 'Worthy is the Lamb that was slain' is the Lamb of 5:6-9 who redeemed by his blood, Jesus Christ who loosed us in his blood (1:5).
readings.second: 'Worthy is the Lamb that was slain' is the Lamb of 5:6-9 who 'redeemed us to God by thy blood', as 1:5 says of Jesus Christ; 5:5 with 22:16.

readings.first: 'unto the Lamb' set beside 'him that sitteth upon the throne' is the slain Lamb of 5:6-12 who redeemed by blood, Jesus Christ of 1:5.
readings.second: Blessing is given 'unto him that sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb', the slain Lamb of 5:6-9, identified through 5:5 and 22:16 'I Jesus ... the root ... of David'.

readings.first: 'the Lamb opened one of the seals' is the Lamb who took the book in 5:7, slain and redeeming by blood (5:9), Jesus Christ of 1:5.
readings.second: 'the Lamb opened one of the seals' is the slain Lamb of 5:6-9, the Root of David of 5:5, which 22:16 claims: 'I Jesus ... the root ... of David'.

readings.first: 'when he had opened the fifth seal' is the Lamb who 'opened one of the seals' (6:1), Jesus Christ of 1:5 and 5:9; only the verb 'He opened' carries the person.
readings.second: 'when he had opened the fifth seal' continues 6:1 'the Lamb opened one of the seals', the Lamb of 5:5-9 (22:16 'I Jesus'); Greek has only the verb 'He opened'.

readings.first: 'the wrath of the Lamb' is the slain Lamb of 5:6-12 who redeemed by blood, Jesus Christ of 1:5; 'him that sitteth on the throne' is set apart from him.
readings.second: They hide 'from the wrath of the Lamb', the slain Lamb of 5:6-9 who opens the seals (6:1), identified through 5:5 and 22:16 'I Jesus ... the root ... of David'.

readings.first: 'sealed ... of all the tribes of the children of Israel': the nation, counted by its tribes.
readings.second: 'sealed ... of all the tribes of the children of Israel': the nation by its tribes.

readings.first: 'Of the tribe of Gad were sealed twelve thousand': the tribe as a body.
readings.second: 'Of the tribe of Gad were sealed twelve thousand': members of the tribe sealed.

readings.first: 'Of the tribe of Reuben were sealed twelve thousand': the tribe as one of the twelve sealed.
readings.second: 'Of the tribe of Reuben were sealed twelve thousand': the tribe as a body among 'all the tribes of the children of Israel' (7:4).

readings.first: 'Of the tribe of Aser were sealed twelve thousand': a tribe sealed in number.
readings.second: 'Of the tribe of Aser were sealed twelve thousand': one of 'all the tribes of the children of Israel' (v.4).

readings.first: 'Of the tribe of Issachar were sealed twelve thousand': the tribe as a body, counted.
readings.second: 'Of the tribe of Issachar were sealed twelve thousand': the tribe as a body.

readings.first: 'Of the tribe of Levi were sealed twelve thousand': the tribe counted with the others.
readings.second: 'Of the tribe of Levi were sealed twelve thousand': one of the tribes counted among the sealed.

readings.first: 'Of the tribe of Simeon were sealed twelve thousand': the tribe among those sealed.
readings.second: 'Of the tribe of Simeon were sealed twelve thousand': the tribe as a body among the sealed of Israel (7:4).

readings.first: 'Of the tribe of Benjamin were sealed twelve thousand': the tribe as a body, a sealed number from it.
readings.second: 'Of the tribe of Benjamin were sealed twelve thousand': members of the tribe sealed as a body.

readings.first: 'Of the tribe of Zabulon were sealed twelve thousand': the tribe among those sealed.
readings.second: 'Of the tribe of Zabulon were sealed twelve thousand': the tribe as a body among the sealed of Israel (7:4).

readings.first: 'before the Lamb': the Lamb that is slain and redeems by blood (5:9, 12:11) is Jesus Christ who 'washed us from our sins in his own blood' (1:5).
readings.second: 'before the Lamb' names the Lamb whose blood redeems (REV 5:9, 7:14), as Jesus Christ 'washed us from our sins in his own blood' (REV 1:5); 'the Lamb' is his title in Revelation.

readings.first: 'Salvation to our God ... and unto the Lamb': the Lamb is the slain one of 5:6-9, matched to Jesus Christ's blood in 1:5 and 'his Christ' beside the Lamb's blood in 12:10-11.
readings.second: 'unto the Lamb' is the slain Lamb who redeemed by his blood (REV 5:9), matching Jesus Christ who 'washed us from our sins in his own blood' (REV 1:5).

readings.first: 'made them white in the blood of the Lamb': the Lamb's blood washes, as Jesus Christ 'washed us from our sins in his own blood' (1:5); the Lamb is the slain one of 5:9.
readings.second: 'made them white in the blood of the Lamb' parallels REV 1:5, where Jesus Christ 'washed us from our sins in his own blood'; the Lamb is his title here.

readings.first: 'the Lamb which is in the midst of the throne shall feed them' is the Lamb of 5:6, slain and redeeming by blood (5:9), i.e. Jesus Christ (1:5).
readings.second: 'the Lamb which is in the midst of the throne' is the slain Lamb of REV 5:6-9 whose blood redeems, as Jesus Christ's does in REV 1:5; 'he... shall feed them' continues it.

readings.first: 'when he had opened the seventh seal': only a verb ending; the opener of the seals is the Lamb (5:5-9, 6:1 'when the Lamb opened one of the seals'), named in 7:17 just before.
readings.second: 'when he had opened the seventh seal' has only the verb; the opener of the seals is the Lamb (REV 6:1 'when the Lamb opened one of the seals'), whose title stands for Jesus in Revelation.

readings.first: 'a great red dragon' is 'that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan' of 12:9, 'the great dragon' cast out to the earth.
readings.second: 'a great red dragon' is the one 12:9 identifies: 'the great dragon ... that old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan'.

readings.first: 'by the blood of the Lamb' beside 12:10 'the power of his Christ': the Lamb slain and redeeming by blood (5:9) is Jesus Christ (1:5).
readings.second: 'by the blood of the Lamb' follows 'the power of his Christ' (12:10) and echoes REV 1:5, Jesus Christ who washed us 'in his own blood'.

readings.first: 'the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world': the slain Lamb of 5:6,9 is the one who 'washed us from our sins in his own blood' (1:5), Jesus Christ.
readings.second: 'the book of life of the Lamb slain' names the slain Lamb of REV 5:9, whose blood redeems as Jesus Christ's does in REV 1:5.

readings.first: 'a Lamb stood on the mount Sion, and with him ... having his Father's name': the Lamb of 5:6-9 and 12:10-11, who is Jesus Christ (1:5); his Father is named here.
readings.second: 'a Lamb stood on the mount Sion... having his Father's name' is the Lamb of Revelation, whose blood redeems (5:9) as Jesus Christ's does (1:5); him and his follow it.

readings.first: 'in the presence of the Lamb': the same Lamb as 14:1,4, slain and redeeming (5:9), who is Jesus Christ (1:5).
readings.second: 'in the presence of the Lamb' names the Lamb, the title Revelation gives the one who redeemed by his blood (5:9), as Jesus Christ did (1:5).

readings.first: 'the song of the Lamb' set beside the song of Moses: the Lamb of the book is Jesus Christ, the slain redeemer (5:9, 1:5).
readings.second: 'the song of the Lamb' names the Lamb, Revelation's title for the one redeeming by his blood (5:9, cf. Jesus Christ in 1:5); 'Lord God Almighty' addressed after is God.

readings.first: 'the Lamb shall overcome them: for he is Lord of lords, and King of kings'; the Lamb is the slain one (5:9), i.e. Jesus Christ (1:5), who is also 'King of kings' in 19:16.
readings.second: 'make war with the Lamb, and the Lamb shall overcome them: for he is Lord of lords' is the Lamb of Revelation, whose blood redeems (5:9) as Jesus Christ's does (1:5).

readings.first: 'the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife': the Lamb is the slain one of 5:6-9, Jesus Christ (1:5); the same Lamb is meant in 21:9 'the Lamb's wife'.
readings.second: 'the marriage of the Lamb is come, and his wife' names the Lamb, Revelation's title for the redeemer by blood (5:9, 1:5 Jesus Christ); 'give honour to him' is God of 19:6.

readings.first: 'the marriage supper of the Lamb': the Lamb is the slain redeemer of 5:9, Jesus Christ (1:5), whose marriage is announced in 19:7.
readings.second: 'the marriage supper of the Lamb' names the Lamb, Revelation's title for the one who redeemed by his blood (5:9), as Jesus Christ did (1:5).

readings.first: 'he that sat upon him was called Faithful and True': the rider's titles fit Jesus Christ 'the faithful witness' (1:5, 3:14), and he is King of kings and Lord of lords (19:16) as the Lamb is (17:14).
readings.second: The rider 'called Faithful and True' bears 'KING OF KINGS, AND LORD OF LORDS' (19:16), the Lamb's title in 17:14, and matches 'Jesus Christ, who is the faithful witness' (1:5, 3:14).

readings.first: 'his name is called The Word of God' names the rider of 19:11, who is King of kings and Lord of lords (19:16) like the Lamb (17:14), Jesus Christ; his 'vesture dipped in blood' fits the Lamb's blood.
readings.second: 'his name is called The Word of God' names the rider of 19:11, who bears the Lamb's title 'KING OF KINGS' (19:16, 17:14) and is 'Faithful and True' as Jesus Christ is 'the faithful witness' (1:5).

readings.first: 'the bride, the Lamb's wife': the Lamb is the slain Lamb of 5:6-9 and 19:7, Jesus Christ (1:5).
readings.second: 'the bride, the Lamb's wife' names the Lamb, Revelation's title for the one who redeemed by his blood (5:9), as Jesus Christ did (1:5).

readings.first: 'the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel': the nation, by its tribes, on the gates.
readings.second: 'the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel': the nation's tribes written on the gates.

readings.first: 'the twelve apostles of the Lamb': the Lamb is the slain Lamb of 5:6-9, Jesus Christ (1:5), whose sent ones are apostles.
readings.second: 'the twelve apostles of the Lamb' names the Lamb, Revelation's title for the one who redeemed by his blood (5:9), as Jesus Christ did (1:5).

readings.first: 'the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple of it': the Lamb is the slain one of 5:6-9, Jesus Christ (1:5), named beside God.
readings.second: 'the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple of it' names the Lamb beside God, Revelation's title for the redeemer by blood (5:9), as Jesus Christ is (1:5).

readings.first: 'the Lamb is the light thereof': the Lamb, distinct from God whose glory lightens the city, is the slain Lamb of 5:6-9, Jesus Christ (1:5).
readings.second: 'the Lamb is the light thereof' names the Lamb, Revelation's title for the one who redeemed by his blood (5:9), as Jesus Christ did (1:5).

readings.first: 'the Lamb's book of life': the Lamb of 13:8 and 21:9, the slain Lamb of 5:9, is Jesus Christ (1:5).
readings.second: 'the Lamb's book of life' names the Lamb, Revelation's title for the one who redeemed by his blood (5:9), as Jesus Christ did (1:5).

readings.first: 'the throne of God and of the Lamb': the Lamb beside God on the throne (cf. 5:6,13) is the slain Lamb, Jesus Christ (1:5).
readings.second: 'the throne of God and of the Lamb' names the Lamb, Revelation's title for the one who redeemed by his blood (5:9), as Jesus Christ did (1:5).

readings.first: 'the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in it': the Lamb is the slain Lamb of 5:6-9, Jesus Christ (1:5).
readings.second: 'the throne of God and of the Lamb' names the Lamb; 'his servants shall serve him' may be God or the Lamb, so only 'the Lamb' is given.

readings.first: 'I am Alpha and Omega, the first and the last' follows 'behold, I come quickly' (22:12) and leads to 'I Jesus' (22:16), and 1:17-18 gives 'the first and the last' to the one who was dead; yet 1:8, 21:6 give 'Alpha and Omega' to God.
readings.second: The speaker continues 22:12 'I come quickly', whom 22:16 'I Jesus' and 22:20 'Surely I come quickly... come, Lord Jesus' identify; yet 1:8 gives 'Alpha and Omega' to the Lord God.
readings.settled: Kept, of the verse only: the speaker of 'I come quickly' (22:12) says 'I Jesus have sent mine angel' (22:16) and 'Surely I come quickly' (22:20).
